llr.text: `check_semantics` shall reject any HLR id that does not match the `^HLR-\d{3,}$` pattern and any LLR id that does not match the `^LLR-[A-Z0-9]+-\d{2,}$` pattern as a hard error so that ID format breaks CI rather than degrading silently into a coverage gap.

`check_semantics` shall report every duplicate `HLR-NNN` or `LLR-XXX-NN` id as an error naming both the duplicate id and (where available) the line of the offending element so the user can navigate directly to it.

`check_semantics` shall resolve every `<trace target="HLR" ref="…"/>` against the set of HLR ids and every `<trace target="LLR" ref="…"/>` against the set of LLR ids; an unresolved reference shall produce an error finding that quotes the missing id and the citing element so the user can fix it without searching the file.

`check_semantics` shall classify `<trace target="SDD" ref="…"/>` references as warnings (rather than errors) when the `ref` does not look like a dotted SDD section id (`^\d+(\.\d+)*$`), reflecting that SDD sections are weakly resolvable until the renderer's section catalogue is reached.

`check_semantics` shall compute coverage gaps from the parsed tree — HLRs with no LLR or test linking to them, LLRs with no test linking to them — and shall emit one warning per gap so that the rendered Traceability Matrix and the Problems panel see the same set.

`check_semantics` shall verify that every document id referenced by a Jinja2 template under `tools/templates/` has a matching `<metadata><document id="…">` entry; missing entries shall be reported as errors and duplicate document ids shall be reported as errors.

check_semantics shall emit a mixed-prefix warning when a <function> element contains LLRs whose dominant id prefix (≥4 members) coexists with a minority prefix (≤2 members), indicating AI-generated ids that did not adopt the established naming convention.

function.title: `serve` and `handle_request` ([tools/project_io.py](../tools/project_io.py))
function.name: serve
function.intro: The JSON-RPC 2.0 dispatch loop and the per-method handler dispatcher that together implement the long-running sidecar.

llr.text: `serve` shall read line-delimited JSON requests from stdin and write line-delimited JSON responses to stdout, flushing after each response, so a client that opens stdin/stdout pipes and writes one request per line gets exactly one response per line in the same order.
`serve` shall ignore blank input lines and shall exit cleanly with status 0 on EOF so the client can shut the sidecar down by closing stdin without needing a dedicated `shutdown` method.

`handle_request` shall return a JSON-RPC error with code `-32700` (parse error) for any input that is not valid JSON, with code `-32600` (invalid request) when `method` is missing or non-string, and with code `-32601` (method not found) when the method name is unknown — exactly matching the JSON-RPC 2.0 specification.

`handle_request` shall return code `-32602` (invalid params) for `ValueError` raised by a handler, code `-32000` (application error) for `ProjectXmlError`, and code `-32603` (internal error) for any other uncaught exception so that user-fixable errors are distinguishable from sidecar bugs by the client.

`handle_request` shall correlate every response with its request by echoing the request's `id` field verbatim (including `null`), and shall suppress the response entirely when the request is a JSON-RPC notification (`jsonrpc=="2.0"` and no `id` key).

`handle_request` shall dispatch every method through the `METHODS` registry rather than via per-method `if`/`elif` branches so adding a new method is a single registry-table edit and the JSON-RPC error machinery applies uniformly.

The `METHODS` registry shall map `lint`, `render`, `parse_to_json`, and `init_project` to thin wrappers around the corresponding `tools/render_doc.py` / `tools/lint_project.py` library functions; no method handler shall reimplement parsing, rendering, or linting logic in `project_io.py`.

function.title: `activate` ([tools/vscode-project-xml/src/extension.ts](../tools/vscode-project-xml/src/extension.ts))
function.name: activate
function.intro: The VS Code extension entry point that wires every Phase 1-2 surface (sidecar client, tree view, lint diagnostics, code lenses, render & preview, reveal-in-XML) into a single activation pass.

llr.text: `activate` shall construct the `ProjectIoClient`, register every contributed command, and create the `Project Spec` tree view, the lint `DiagnosticCollection`, the `tracer-preview:` content provider, and the coverage code-lens provider — pushing each onto `context.subscriptions` so they are torn down deterministically on extension deactivate.

`activate` shall register the `Project Spec` `OutputChannel` first and pass it to every component that may report a sidecar or parse failure so the user can diagnose interpreter / workspace problems without leaving the editor.

`activate` shall subscribe to `vscode.workspace.onDidSaveTextDocument` and, when the saved document is the configured `Project.xml`, refresh the tree, refresh the code-lens cache, optionally re-run `lint` (gated on `projectXml.autoLintOnChange`), and optionally invalidate the preview cache (gated on `projectXml.previewOnSave`).

trace.name: Lint Diagnostics in the Problems Panel

llr.text: The extension manifest shall declare `redhat.vscode-xml` as an `extensionDependencies` entry and `untrustedWorkspaces.supported = "limited"` so XSD-backed XML editing comes for free and the deterministic Phase 1-2 surfaces remain available in untrusted workspaces while AI surfaces (Phase 5) can gate themselves off.

trace.name: AI Surfaces Disabled in Untrusted Workspaces

function.title: `ProjectIoClient` ([tools/vscode-project-xml/src/sidecar.ts](../tools/vscode-project-xml/src/sidecar.ts))
function.name: ProjectIoClient
function.intro: The long-running JSON-RPC 2.0 client wrapping `tools/project_io.py`. Every TypeScript surface (tree, diagnostics, lenses, render commands, preview content provider) routes through it.

llr.text: `ProjectIoClient` shall spawn `tools/project_io.py` lazily on first request — never during construction — so importing the module does not require a Python interpreter to be installed and `activate` stays cheap.

`ProjectIoClient.request` shall correlate every JSON-RPC response with its sender by allocating a monotonically-increasing numeric `id`, parking the resolver in a pending-map, and resolving / rejecting it when the line with the matching `id` arrives on stdout — so multiple in-flight requests do not deadlock.

`ProjectIoClient` shall reject every pending request with the same exit error when the sidecar process exits unexpectedly, and shall surface JSON-RPC error responses as `SidecarError(code, message)` so callers can switch on the JSON-RPC error code without parsing message text.

`ProjectIoClient` shall pipe every byte the sidecar writes to stderr into the `Project Spec` `OutputChannel` prefixed with `[sidecar:stderr]`, so Python tracebacks are visible to the user without leaving the editor.

`ProjectIoClient.dispose` shall close the sidecar's stdin and kill the child process, and the same cleanup shall run automatically on extension deactivate via the `context.subscriptions` machinery so the sidecar never outlives the extension.

`ProjectIoClient` shall pick the Python interpreter from the `projectXml.pythonPath` setting first and fall back to `python3` (POSIX) or `python` (Windows) so users with a project venv can point the sidecar at it without editing the extension source.

function.title: `ProjectSpecProvider` ([tools/vscode-project-xml/src/treeView/ProjectSpecProvider.ts](../tools/vscode-project-xml/src/treeView/ProjectSpecProvider.ts))
function.name: ProjectSpecProvider
function.intro: The Phase 1 hand-written tree provider that contributes the `Project Spec` Activity Bar view rooted at `Project.xml`. Phase 2.5 will rewrite the per-payload builders to walk the schema-driven hint registry.

llr.text: `ProjectSpecProvider.getChildren` shall return one root `ProjectSpecNode` per top-level payload (HLRs, LLRs, Tests, SDD, STP) when invoked with no element, with each root labelled with a count derived from the parsed tree (e.g. `HLRs (45)`).

`ProjectSpecProvider` shall populate the tree by calling `ProjectIoClient.parseToJson` exactly once per refresh and caching the result; `refresh()` shall clear the cache and fire `onDidChangeTreeData` so VS Code re-requests the children.

Every leaf `ProjectSpecNode` mapping to a real `<hlr>`, `<llr>`, `<test>`, or `<module>` element shall carry a `RevealLocator` payload `{tag, attr?, value}` and shall set `contextValue = "revealable"` so the Reveal-in-XML command and the context menu can target it precisely.

When `parse_to_json` fails, `ProjectSpecProvider.getChildren` shall return a single error node (themed with `error` icon) bearing the error message rather than throwing, so the tree still renders and the user sees an actionable explanation in the Activity Bar.

After the typed and generic builders have populated the tree roots, `ProjectSpecProvider.buildTopLevel` shall invoke `decorateTooltips(roots, project)` from [coverageTooltips.ts](../tools/vscode-project-xml/src/treeView/coverageTooltips.ts) so every leaf whose `RevealLocator.tag` is `hlr`, `llr`, or `test` carries a Markdown tooltip computed from the same `flat_hlrs` / `flat_llrs` / `flat_tests` payload already returned by `parse_to_json` — no second sidecar round-trip and no parallel coverage index.

Each tooltip emitted by `decorateTooltips` shall be a trusted `vscode.MarkdownString` (`isTrusted = true`) whose body lists upstream and downstream items as bullet points, with each bullet rendered as a `[label](command:projectXml.revealInXml?<encoded-locator>)` link so a single click in the hover surface jumps to the cited element via the existing `revealInXml` code path; leaves with neither upstream nor downstream items shall render an explicit "No traces yet." / "No downstream LLRs or tests yet." line rather than an empty tooltip so coverage gaps are visible from hover. Test entries in the tooltip lists shall include the test's parent file path (`ParsedTest.file`) as a sublabel, and the Test tooltip header shall display the file path alongside the test name. Tooltip text shall be rendered without Markdown backslash-escaping so that underscores and other characters in names and paths appear cleanly in both inline and code-span contexts.

Every leaf `ProjectSpecNode` whose `RevealLocator` identifies a concrete payload element (`<hlr>`, `<llr>`, `<test>`, `<module>`, or any element carrying a `<ui:form>` annotation) shall set `TreeItem.command` to `projectXml.editPayload` with the node's locator as argument, so that double-clicking the leaf in VS Code's tree view opens the schema-driven popup edit dialog for that element. The command wiring shall be generic — derived from the hint registry — so new payload kinds surface as double-clickable leaves with no extension code change.

The Project Spec tree view title bar shall contribute a dropdown menu (via `contributes.menus["view/title"]`) exposing, in order: Refresh, Run Linter, Render All Documents, Resolve Merge Conflicts, and Initialize Project.xml. The first three shall appear in a single group (`1_actions`), and the last two in a second group (`2_project`) separated by a visual divider. Each entry shall set `shortTitle` on its command definition to display the exact label listed above. The Refresh command shall additionally remain as a clickable icon button in the `navigation` group so the tree toolbar keeps its quick-access refresh affordance.

After building the tree nodes, buildTopLevel shall invoke propagateBadges which walks bottom-up and sets a coloured ThemeIcon (error=red, warning=yellow via list.warningForeground ThemeColor) on every parent node whose descendants carry a badge. This allows users to identify subtrees containing findings without expanding every node.

trace.name: Coverage Status Badges in the Tree

llr.text: `buildStpDescriptor` shall render the STP tree group as a collapsible node labelled `STP (N fixtures)` whose children are one leaf per `<fixture>` element under `<stp>/<integration_environment>`. Each fixture leaf shall carry an `editArgs` with `type='StpFixture'`, `basePath='/stp/integration_environment/fixture[name=X]'`, and `formData` containing `name` and `source` fields, and shall set `contextValue` to `stpGroup` on the parent so the context menu exposes the `addStpFixture` command. When no STP section exists the node shall render as `STP (empty)` with no children and no context value.

function.title: `LintDiagnosticsProvider` ([tools/vscode-project-xml/src/diagnostics/LintDiagnosticsProvider.ts](../tools/vscode-project-xml/src/diagnostics/LintDiagnosticsProvider.ts))
function.name: LintDiagnosticsProvider
function.intro: Mirrors lint findings from `project_io.lint` into a VS Code `DiagnosticCollection` over `Project.xml`. Phase 2.5's stable-`code` retrofit and Quick Fix table layer on top of this Phase 1 surface.

llr.text: `LintDiagnosticsProvider.run` shall call `ProjectIoClient.lint` with the configured `xml_path` and (when set) `xsd_path`, and shall replace the entire `DiagnosticCollection` for `Project.xml` on success so the Problems panel reflects the latest lint state without requiring the user to clear stale entries.

trace.name: Lint Diagnostics in the Problems Panel

llr.text: `LintDiagnosticsProvider.publish` shall map each `Findings.errors` entry to `DiagnosticSeverity.Error`, each warning to `DiagnosticSeverity.Warning`, and each note to `DiagnosticSeverity.Information` — preserving every finding verbatim so warnings are never silently downgraded or hidden.

trace.name: Lint Diagnostics in the Problems Panel

llr.text: Each `Diagnostic` shall be anchored to a best-effort range computed by `rangeForFinding(doc, message)` (HLR/LLR id token first, quoted attribute value second, `<element>` mention third, file head as fallback) and shall set `source = "projectXml"` so users can filter the Problems panel to the linter's output.

trace.name: Lint Diagnostics in the Problems Panel

llr.text: When `ProjectIoClient.lint` rejects (interpreter missing, sidecar exited), `LintDiagnosticsProvider.run` shall publish a single top-of-file `Error` diagnostic carrying the failure message rather than swallowing the rejection silently, so the user sees the failure in the Problems panel and the `Project Spec` `OutputChannel` simultaneously.

trace.name: Lint Diagnostics in the Problems Panel

function.title: `revealInXml` and `locator` helpers ([tools/vscode-project-xml/src/](../tools/vscode-project-xml/src/))
function.name: revealInXml
function.intro: The Phase 1 jump-to-element command, plus the regex-based locator helpers it uses to range XML elements without parsing the file in TypeScript.

llr.text: `revealInXml` shall accept either a `ProjectSpecNode` (from a tree-view context-menu invocation) or a bare `RevealLocator` (from the code-lens click path) and shall dispatch through `findIdRange` / `findAttrRange` / `findElementRange` so every caller takes the same locator code path.

`findIdRange` shall match `<TAG ... id="ID">` via regex, return a `vscode.Range` over the `id="..."` attribute value (not the whole tag), and never fall through to a wrong element when two elements share an id substring (the regex anchors on `\bid="ID"`).

When the locator cannot find the requested element, `revealInXml` shall still open `Project.xml` in a non-preview editor and shall surface a warning toast describing what was not found (`<llr id="LLR-PCL-04"> not found in Project.xml`) so the user has both the file and an actionable explanation.

`rangeForFinding` shall scan a finding message for `HLR-NNN` ids first, then `LLR-XXX-NN` ids, then quoted attribute values, then `<element>` mentions, and shall return the first hit's range — falling back to the file head only when none match — so diagnostic underlines target the most specific token available.

trace.name: Lint Diagnostics in the Problems Panel

function.title: `renderAndPreview` and `MarkdownPreviewProvider` ([tools/vscode-project-xml/src/](../tools/vscode-project-xml/src/))
function.name: renderAndPreview
function.intro: The Phase 2 side-by-side Markdown preview surface: a `tracer-preview:/<doc-id>.md` content provider plus the command that opens it via `markdown.showPreviewToSide`.

llr.text: `renderAndPreview` shall accept an optional `docId` (string or `{docId}` object) argument, prompt the user with a QuickPick over the runtime-discovered document set returned by `loadDocuments(client)` (which calls the sidecar's `list_documents` method) when none is supplied, and refuse with a warning toast when the supplied id is not in the discovered set — never falling through to a partial render and never carrying a hard-coded list of document ids.

`renderAndPreview` shall mark the preview cache stale for the chosen `docId` and then dispatch `vscode.commands.executeCommand("markdown.showPreviewToSide", uri)` so the user always sees content rendered against the current `Project.xml` state, not a cached snapshot.

`MarkdownPreviewProvider` shall register the `tracer-preview` URI scheme via `vscode.workspace.registerTextDocumentContentProvider` and shall serve content for `tracer-preview:/<doc-id>.md` URIs by calling `ProjectIoClient.render` against the template path resolved from the runtime-discovered document set (via `loadDocuments(client)`) — so no preview path ever writes a Markdown file under `doc/` and a brand-new `<metadata><document>` entry yields a working preview pane on next refresh with no source-code edit.

`MarkdownPreviewProvider.markStale(docId?)` shall drop the cached markdown for `docId` (or every tracked preview when called with no argument) and shall fire `onDidChange` for each tracked id so VS Code re-requests content; the on-save handler in `activate` shall call this when `projectXml.previewOnSave` is enabled.

When `ProjectIoClient.render` rejects, `MarkdownPreviewProvider.provideTextDocumentContent` shall return a `# Project Spec preview — render failed` Markdown body quoting the error (and append the failure to the `Project Spec` `OutputChannel`) rather than throwing, so the preview pane always shows actionable text instead of crashing the host.

function.title: `renderAll` and `BASELINE_DOCUMENTS` ([tools/vscode-project-xml/src/](../tools/vscode-project-xml/src/))
function.name: renderAll
function.intro: The Phase 2 batch-regeneration command, plus the single named constant Phase 2.5 will swap for a `list_documents` sidecar call.

llr.text: `renderAll` shall iterate the runtime-discovered document set returned by `loadDocuments(client)` (sourced from the sidecar's `list_documents` method) and shall call `ProjectIoClient.render` for each entry with the `out` parameter set to the resolved `output` path so each generated Markdown is written by the sidecar (never assembled in TypeScript) and so a new `<metadata><document>` entry is rendered automatically on the next `Render All` invocation with no source-code edit.

`renderAll` shall display a progress notification while it runs, shall continue past per-document failures (collecting them into a failure list rather than aborting on the first error), and shall summarise both the success count and the failed document ids in the closing toast.

`renderAll` shall call `MarkdownPreviewProvider.markStale()` (with no argument) at the end of every run so any preview pane the user opened earlier in the session refreshes against the new on-disk state.

The runtime document set in [util/documents.ts](../tools/vscode-project-xml/src/util/documents.ts) shall be sourced exclusively from the sidecar's `list_documents` method via `loadDocuments(client)` (with a per-client cache invalidated on `refresh` and on `Project.xml` save). No TypeScript module shall carry an inline list of document ids; every consumer (the dynamic per-document render commands registered in `activate`, the `renderAll` loop, the `renderAndPreview` QuickPick, the `MarkdownPreviewProvider` lookup) shall import this discovery surface so a new `<metadata><document>` entry yields a working command, preview, and tree node with no source-code edit.

function.title: `CoverageCodeLensProvider` ([tools/vscode-project-xml/src/codeLens/CoverageCodeLensProvider.ts](../tools/vscode-project-xml/src/codeLens/CoverageCodeLensProvider.ts))
function.name: CoverageCodeLensProvider
function.intro: The Phase 2 code-lens provider that decorates `<hlr>`, `<llr>`, and `<test>` elements with coverage status and click-through reveal lenses. Phase 2.5 will replace the hard-coded element selectors with a walk over `ui_hints_index.lenses`.

llr.text: `CoverageCodeLensProvider.provideCodeLenses` shall return code lenses only when the active document's path equals the configured `Project.xml` so other XML files in the workspace are not decorated.

For every `<hlr id="…">` element the provider shall emit a summary lens whose title is `"<n> LLRs · <m> tests"` computed from the parsed tree's `<traces>` blocks (LLRs that trace to this HLR, plus tests that trace to it directly), and the analogous summary for every `<llr>` (`"<n> HLRs · <m> tests"`) and every `<test>` (`"<n> LLRs · <m> HLRs"`).

Each summary lens shall invoke a picker command (`projectXml.codeLens.pickRelated`) that opens a QuickPick over every related element; up to `MAX_INLINE_LENSES` related items shall additionally be emitted as inline `→ <id>` lenses that invoke `projectXml.revealInXml` with the per-related locator so the most common jumps are one click away.

An element with zero related items shall render the summary lens with title `"<n> LLRs · <m> tests — no coverage"` and an empty command so the user sees the gap without being given a useless click target; the provider shall not emit per-related inline lenses in this case.

`CoverageCodeLensProvider` shall cache the parsed project across consecutive `provideCodeLenses` invocations and shall coalesce concurrent in-flight `parseToJson` calls into a single sidecar request, so VS Code's per-keystroke lens-recompute does not fan out into N parallel sidecar calls.

`CoverageCodeLensProvider.refresh` shall drop the parsed-project cache and fire `onDidChangeCodeLenses` so a save (handled in `activate`) refreshes every lens range and label against the new on-disk state.

function.title: `paths` helpers ([tools/vscode-project-xml/src/util/paths.ts](../tools/vscode-project-xml/src/util/paths.ts))
function.name: paths
function.intro: Workspace-path resolution shared by every extension surface. Centralised here so the multi-root case and the `projectXml.*` settings overrides are handled in one place.

llr.text: `getProjectFolder` shall pick the open workspace folder whose root contains the configured `xmlPath` (default `doc/Project.xml`) so the extension works equally for a user who opens the TraceR repo root and for a user who opens a parent multi-root workspace.

`getProjectXmlPath`, `getXsdPath`, `getToolsDir`, and `getProjectIoScript` shall each resolve their result against `getProjectFolder()` when given a relative setting, return the value verbatim when given an absolute path, and return `undefined` only when no workspace folder is open — so callers can fail loudly with a single null check.

`describeWorkspaceState` shall return a single human-readable sentence explaining why path resolution failed (no workspace folder open, or `Project.xml` not found in any folder) so the sidecar's startup error message is actionable.

function.title: `list_documents` and the document-metadata contract ([tools/render_doc.py](../tools/render_doc.py), [tools/project_io.py](../tools/project_io.py), [tools/project.xsd](../tools/project.xsd), [tools/lint_project.py](../tools/lint_project.py))
function.name: list_documents
function.intro: The Phase 2.5 schema-driven discovery surface. `<metadata><document>` is the single declaration site for every generated document; `render_doc.list_documents` exposes the resolved set; `project_io.list_documents` ships it over JSON-RPC; the linter and the XSD enforce the contract.

llr.text: `tools/project.xsd` shall accept (but not require) `template` and `output` attributes on `<metadata><document>`. When omitted, the conventional defaults `tools/templates/<id>.md.j2` (template) and the value of the `source` attribute (output) shall apply, so existing files require no edit; when present, they shall override the conventional paths verbatim, so a project can ship a generated document whose template lives outside `tools/templates/` or whose rendered output writes to a path other than `source`.

`render_doc.list_documents(xml_path)` shall parse `Project.xml` and return one dict per `<metadata><document>` containing at minimum `id`, `title`, `source`, `version`, `date`, `author`, `template`, and `output`, with `template` and `output` resolved against the conventional defaults when the XML omits them — so the JSON-RPC sidecar, the VS Code extension, and any future automation see the same document set without re-implementing the resolution logic.

`project_io.py` shall expose `list_documents` as a JSON-RPC method routed through the `METHODS` registry that returns `{"documents": [...]}` whose entries are exactly the dicts produced by `render_doc.list_documents`, so a TypeScript or external client can discover the document set without spawning a separate Python process.

`tools/lint_project.py` shall derive the set of expected documents from the linted file's own `<metadata><document>` declarations rather than from a hard-coded allow-list. For every declared document whose resolved template (explicit `template=` attribute or the conventional `tools/templates/<id>.md.j2` path) is absent from disk, the linter shall emit a warning with internal code `missing-template` naming both the document id and the missing template path, so an authoring mistake is caught at lint time rather than at first render.

`tools/project.xsd` shall declare `xmlns:ui="urn:tracer:ui:v1"` on its schema root and reserve the `ui:*` attribute space for a future hint registry. The renderer (`render_doc.py`) and the linter (`lint_project.py`) shall not consume `ui:*` attributes, so files that adopt the registry remain renderable and lintable by toolchains that pre-date the hint feature.

function.title: `BadgeIndex` ([tools/vscode-project-xml/src/util/badges.ts](../tools/vscode-project-xml/src/util/badges.ts))
function.name: BadgeIndex
function.intro: Phase 2.5 Slice E: a small projection of the linter's structured `Findings.items[]` output onto the HLR / LLR ids each finding mentions, so the tree provider can decorate the matching leaf nodes with a coverage status badge. The linter remains the single source of truth — the badge set is built each time `lint` runs and replaces any prior set.

llr.text: `buildBadgeIndex(items)` shall iterate the structured lint findings (`severity`, `message`, `code`) returned in `Findings.to_dict()["items"]` and shall record every `HLR-NNN` and `LLR-XXX-NN` id mentioned in each error or warning message under the corresponding tag (`'hlr'`, `'llr'`); notes shall not contribute to the badge set so informational findings do not clutter the tree.

trace.name: Coverage Status Badges in the Tree

llr.text: `BadgeIndex.badgeFor(tag, id)` shall return `'❌'` when any error finding cites the id, `'⚠'` when only warnings do, and `undefined` otherwise; an id cited by both an error and a warning shall always badge as `'❌'` so the most severe state surfaces regardless of finding order.

trace.name: Coverage Status Badges in the Tree

llr.text: `ProjectSpecProvider.setBadges(idx)` shall accept the index produced by `buildBadgeIndex` (or `undefined` to clear), shall drop the cached tree, and shall fire `onDidChangeTreeData` so VS Code re-requests the leaf labels with the new decorations applied; the extension's activate path shall call this method after every `LintDiagnosticsProvider.run()` so the Problems panel and the tree decorations stay in lock-step.

trace.name: Coverage Status Badges in the Tree

llr.text: The tree decoration shall be gated on the `projectXml.showCoverageBadges` setting (boolean, default true). When disabled, `buildTopLevel` shall ignore the stored badge index and emit undecorated labels so a user who prefers an unannotated tree can opt out without losing the underlying Problems-panel output.

trace.name: Coverage Status Badges in the Tree

function.title: UI hint registry ([tools/render_doc.py](../tools/render_doc.py), [tools/vscode-project-xml/src/util/hints.ts](../tools/vscode-project-xml/src/util/hints.ts))
function.name: ui_hints
function.intro: Phase 2.5b activates the reserved `urn:tracer:ui:v1` namespace as a payload-side decoration channel. The XSD accepts arbitrary `ui:*` attributes via `<xs:anyAttribute>` on `<hlr>`, `<llr>`, `<test>`, and `<module>`; the Python renderer projects the recognised subset onto a flat dict surfaced as `.ui` on each parsed node; the VS Code extension consumes that field to decorate tree leaves with VS Code icons and `ThemeColor` tints.

llr.text: `tools/project.xsd` shall declare `<xs:anyAttribute namespace="urn:tracer:ui:v1" processContents="skip"/>` on the `Hlr`, `Llr`, `Test`, and `SddModule` complex types so any number of `ui:*` attributes is accepted on those payload elements without the schema needing to enumerate them, and unknown ui:* attributes pass validation rather than rejecting the file.

`render_doc._ui_hints(elem)` shall extract the recognised hint keys (`icon`, `color`, `group`) from `urn:tracer:ui:v1` attributes via ElementTree's Clark-notation key form (`{urn:tracer:ui:v1}icon`), return a flat dict containing only the keys whose values are non-empty strings, and return `None` when no recognised hint is present so the JSON output distinguishes "no hints" from "an empty hints object" without ambiguity.

`build_hlr`, `build_llr`, `build_test`, and `build_module` shall attach the `_ui_hints(elem)` result as a `ui` field on the `SimpleNamespace` they return, and the flat-list builders inside `load_project` (`flat_hlrs`, `flat_llrs`, `flat_tests`) shall propagate it forward via `getattr(node, "ui", None)` so `parse_project_to_dict` exposes the hints on the same JSON path the VS Code tree provider reads from.

`util/hints.applyHintsToNode(node, hints)` shall be a no-op (returning `false`) when hints is `null`, `undefined`, or carries no non-empty `icon`; otherwise it shall set `node.iconPath = new vscode.ThemeIcon(icon, color ? new vscode.ThemeColor(color) : undefined)` (after trimming whitespace from both fields) and return `true`. The reserved `group` key shall be accepted-and-ignored. `ProjectSpecProvider.buildHlrsNode`, `buildLlrsNode`, `buildTestsNode`, and `buildSddNode` shall invoke this helper on every leaf so hint-decorated nodes look identical regardless of the underlying tag.

function.title: Quick Fix table ([tools/vscode-project-xml/src/codeActions/](../tools/vscode-project-xml/src/codeActions/))
function.name: quickfix
function.intro: Phase 2.5c: a payload-agnostic `CodeActionProvider` whose Quick Fix table is keyed strictly on the stable `Finding.code` values shipped in Phase 2.5 (`broken-trace`, `id-format`, `missing-template`, `no-test`). Every fix uses VS Code `WorkspaceEdit` text edits so the Phase 3 `apply_edit` write path is not required. The provider never branches on payload element name, so a new payload kind that triggers an existing `Finding.code` inherits the Quick Fix surface for free.

llr.text: `LintDiagnosticsProvider.publish` shall mirror each structured `LintFinding`'s optional `code` field onto the corresponding `vscode.Diagnostic.code` so the `QuickFixProvider` can dispatch on the stable token without re-parsing the human message; older sidecar responses lacking the structured `items` list shall fall back to the flat `errors`/`warnings`/`notes` projection unchanged so the diagnostic surface keeps working when the field is absent.

`QuickFixProvider.provideCodeActions` shall iterate the `context.diagnostics`, ignore any whose `source` is not `'projectXml'`, look up the diagnostic's `code` in a static `FIX_TABLE` keyed on the four Phase 2.5 finding codes (`broken-trace`, `id-format`, `missing-template`, `no-test`), and emit one `vscode.CodeAction` per matched diagnostic carrying `kind = QuickFix`, `isPreferred = true`, and a `command` invocation whose arguments forward the diagnostic's URI, range, and message verbatim. The provider source shall not reference any payload element name (HLR / LLR / plan / future), pinning the SDP §8 Phase 2.5c contract.

`codeActions/fixes.ts` shall expose pure helpers for each Quick Fix: message parsers (`parseBrokenTrace`, `parseIdFormat`, `parseMissingTemplate`, `parseNoTest`) that pull just the data the linter prints out of each finding; id allocators (`nextFreeHlrId`, `nextFreeLlrId`) that preserve the zero-padded width of the existing ids; and stub builders (`templateStubContent`, `stubTestFragment`) that produce text the command layer feeds into a `WorkspaceEdit`. None of the helpers shall touch the VS Code API so they remain unit-testable from a plain Node process.

The Quick Fix command bodies in `commands/quickFixes.ts` shall apply their text edits via `vscode.WorkspaceEdit` only — `replace` for `broken-trace` and `id-format`, `createFile` + `insert` for `missing-template`, and `insert` before `</tests>` for `no-test`. None of the Phase 2.5c fixes shall route through the (future) Phase 3 `apply_edit` sidecar method; structural rewrites that need an XSD-validated round trip migrate onto `apply_edit` once Phase 3 lands.

The `broken-trace` Quick Fix shall populate its picker by walking `flat_hlrs` or `flat_llrs` from the parsed tree according to the trace `target` parsed out of the finding message, never by enumerating known payload element names; this lets a future payload that carries `<traces>` over the same `target` namespace inherit the picker without provider edits.

function.title: apply_edit write surface ([tools/project_edit.py](../tools/project_edit.py))
function.name: aed
function.intro: Phase 3: the authoritative write-back primitive for `doc/Project.xml`. `apply_edit` accepts a list of small JSON-Patch-like operations, applies them on a working copy of the parsed tree, runs XSD + linter validation, and only on a clean result rewrites the file via `lxml` so comments, CDATA, attribute order, and whitespace are preserved (HLR-018). On validation failure the on-disk file is byte-identical to its pre-call state and the structured findings are returned to the caller (HLR-019). Every Phase 3 surface that needs to change Project.xml (the form panel, addHlr/addLlr, the structural Quick Fix) routes through this single function so the validate-then-write contract is enforced in exactly one place.

llr.text: `apply_edit(operations, *, xml_path, xsd_path, expect_clean=True)` shall parse `xml_path` with `lxml.etree.XMLParser(remove_blank_text=False, remove_comments=False, strip_cdata=False)` so the in-memory tree retains every comment, CDATA section, and inter-element whitespace from the source; new text bodies whose value contains markup-significant characters (`<`, `>`, `&`, markdown links/code) shall be wrapped in `etree.CDATA` so subsequent re-renders preserve the formatting (HLR-018).

`apply_edit` shall write the candidate output to a sibling temp file in the same directory as `xml_path`, run `lint_project.lint` on the temp file, and on a finding of severity `error` (or any XSD failure) when `expect_clean` is true return an `ApplyEditResult(ok=False, written=False, findings=…)` *without* touching `xml_path`. The on-disk bytes of `xml_path` shall be byte-identical to its pre-call state on every failure path (HLR-019).

`apply_edit` shall accept a tiny path grammar (`/section/tag[k=v]/@attr`, `.../tag` for child text bodies, `.../tag/-` for an append slot) and three operation kinds (`replace`, `add`, `remove`). Element values shall use the `@attr` / bare-key convention (`@id`, `@name` for attributes; bare keys for child elements with list values for repeated children). The grammar shall be expressive enough to drive every Phase 3 surface (form submission, addHlr/addLlr, the no-test Quick Fix) without a richer JSON Patch implementation.

`apply_edit` shall replace `xml_path` with the validated candidate via `os.replace(tmp_path, xml_path)` so the swap is atomic on POSIX file systems — a crash mid-write cannot leave the user with a half-rewritten Project.xml (HLR-019).

The sidecar shall expose `apply_edit`, `form_schema`, and `next_free_id` JSON-RPC methods backed by the helpers in `project_edit.py`. The TS client (`ProjectIoClient.applyEdit`, `.formSchema`, `.nextFreeId`) shall forward params verbatim and return the structured result so the form panel and Quick Fix layer share one transport.

After applying operations and before lint validation, apply_edit shall re-parse the serialized candidate with remove_blank_text=True and apply etree.indent(space=" ") so that AI-appended elements receive the same 2-space indentation as hand-authored content. The beautifier shall preserve CDATA sections and comments and shall be idempotent (a second pass produces byte-identical output).

When a replace operation targets @id on an <hlr> or <llr> element, apply_edit shall iterate all <trace> elements in the document and update any whose ref attribute matches the old id to the new id, so that renaming a requirement id does not break traceability links.

function.title: Form panel webview ([tools/vscode-project-xml/src/forms/](../tools/vscode-project-xml/src/forms/))
function.name: frm
function.intro: Phase 3 (HLR-026): a payload-agnostic form panel that edits a single `<hlr>` or `<llr>` using `react-jsonschema-form`. The schema is derived at runtime from the relevant XSD subtree plus the `ui:form` field hints in the Phase 2.5b ui_hints_index — there is no per-payload form code. The panel sends a JSON Patch through `apply_edit`, prompts to save dirty buffers before mutating the file, and renders inline validation findings on rejection so the user can correct the form and retry.

llr.text: `derive_form_schema(type_name, *, xsd_path, refs)` shall walk the named complex type's `<xs:appinfo>/<ui:form>` block from the XSD plus the attribute `use` flags and return `{schema, uiSchema, fields, type}`. Field `kind` values (`text`, `textarea`, `cdata`, `enum`, `ref:HLR/LLR/SDD`) shall map to RJSF widgets (`text`, `textarea`, `select`); the `<traces>` subtree shall surface as an array of `{target, ref, name?}` rows whose `ref` selector is populated from the `refs` snapshot when supplied. Adding a new payload kind shall require zero changes to the deriver.

`FormPanelProvider.open` shall first check whether `doc/Project.xml` is open in the editor with unsaved changes; if so it shall prompt the user with a modal warning ("Save and Continue" / "Cancel") and abort the open on cancel. This guards against silently overwriting in-progress edits when the form posts back through `apply_edit`.

`buildOperations({basePath, appendPath}, formData)` shall translate a form submission into the JSON Patch list the sidecar's `apply_edit` accepts. In add mode (no `basePath`) it shall emit a single `add` op against `appendPath`; in edit mode it shall emit one `replace` per attribute (`/@id`, `/@name`) and one `replace` per child (text body, `/traces`). The function shall be a pure helper exported separately from the panel class so the path-shape contract is unit-testable without the VS Code API.

The form webview bundle (`dist/formPanel.js`) shall be produced by a second esbuild entry pointing at `src/forms/webview/formMain.tsx` and shall load `react`, `react-dom`, and `@rjsf/core` + `@rjsf/validator-ajv8` as in-bundle dependencies. The CSP set in `FormPanelProvider`'s HTML shall pin the script to a per-load nonce so no other script can run inside the webview.

When the form panel opens in edit mode, `FormPanelProvider.open` shall compute an inline coverage summary from the current `parse_to_json` result and include it in the `init` message. For HLRs the summary shall list downstream LLRs and direct tests; for LLRs it shall list upstream HLRs and verifying tests; for tests it shall list upstream HLRs and LLRs; for SDD modules it shall list HLRs that trace to the module's path. Each related-item entry shall be a clickable link that posts an `openForm` message with the target's locator so the extension host opens that item's edit form via `resolveFormParams`. Test entries in the HLR and LLR coverage sections shall include the test's parent file path (from `ParsedTest.file`) as a clickable sublabel that posts an `openFile` message so clicking it opens the test source file in the editor; the test's own coverage summary shall include the file path when available. Coverage computation shall reuse `buildCoverageIndex` from `treeView/coverageTooltips.ts` and shall be best-effort — a failure shall not prevent the form from opening.

When the form panel opens in edit mode for an HLR, LLR, or Test, the `formData` passed to the webview shall include a `traces` array populated from the element's parsed `<traces>` block so existing trace rows appear pre-filled and editable. The RJSF `Form` component shall receive a `translateString` callback that maps `TranslatableString.AddItemButton` to `"Add Trace"` so the array-add button displays clear labelling; all other translatable strings shall fall through to the RJSF default.

`snapshotRefIds()` shall collect SDD section references by scanning `parsed.flat_hlrs` traces where `trace.target === 'SDD'`, building a sorted set of unique ref values (e.g. `"2.2"`, `"3"`, `"8"`), and passing them as `out.SDD` alongside the existing HLR and LLR id lists. This populates the `ref` dropdown in the HLR trace-editing form so users can select SDD section targets without manual entry.

`resolveFormParams(parsed, locator)` shall walk the nested project structure (`hlrs`, `llrs`, `tests`, `sdd`, `stp`) to resolve a `{tag, value}` coverage locator into an `OpenFormParams` object containing the `type`, `basePath`, and pre-populated `initial` data. Supported tags are `hlr`, `llr`, `test`, `module`, and `fixture`; unrecognised tags or missing items shall return `undefined`. The extension host's `openForm` message handler shall call `resolveFormParams` and open a new form panel for the resolved item so coverage-hint clicks navigate directly to the target's edit form.

When the SDD module edit form opens (via `editPayload` or `resolveFormParams`), the `formData` / `initial` object passed to the webview shall include all child element fields declared in the XSD `<ui:form>` annotation (`purpose`, `responsibility`, `data_structures`, `algorithm`) in addition to the attribute fields (`path`, `title`). Multi-valued children (e.g. multiple `<responsibility>` elements) shall be joined with newline separators into a single string so the textarea widget displays them as a block.

The trace-editing ref enum in derive_form_schema shall contain the union of all known ids across every target kind (HLR, LLR, SDD) so that a Test tracing directly to an HLR still displays a populated dropdown and the RJSF select widget always has options regardless of which target is selected.

buildReplaceOperations shall emit the @id replace operation last in the operations array so that all other field updates (text, traces) resolve against the original id in the basePath predicate before the rename changes the element identity.

function.title: Add / edit commands ([tools/vscode-project-xml/src/commands/forms.ts](../tools/vscode-project-xml/src/commands/forms.ts))
function.name: add
function.intro: Phase 3: `projectXml.addHlr`, `projectXml.addLlr`, and `projectXml.editPayload` open the schema-driven form panel for new and existing payload nodes. The add commands prompt the user to pick a section/function, allocate the next-free id via the sidecar, and open a blank form against the corresponding append slot; `editPayload` re-uses the same panel in edit mode.

llr.text: `addHlr` shall list every `<hlrs>/<section>` from the parsed tree in a `vscode.QuickPick`, ask the sidecar for the next-free `HLR-NNN`, and open `FormPanelProvider` against `/hlrs/section[number=N]/hlr/-` for the picked section. `addLlr` shall do the same against `<llrs>/<function>` (using the function's `name` for the LLR prefix and asking the sidecar for the next-free `LLR-PREFIX-NN`). Adding a new section or function shall therefore surface a new add target with no extension code change (HLR-005).

The Phase 2.5c `no-test` Quick Fix shall route through `ProjectIoClient.applyEdit` (rather than `WorkspaceEdit.insert` before `</tests>`) so the new `<test>` element passes the XSD + linter gate before the file is rewritten. The other three Phase 2.5c fixes (`broken-trace`, `id-format`, `missing-template`) shall remain on `WorkspaceEdit` because they only mutate flat text and stay usable on dirty buffers.

function.title: Form variants for SDD/STP/Test payloads ([tools/vscode-project-xml/src/forms/FormPanelProvider.ts](../tools/vscode-project-xml/src/forms/FormPanelProvider.ts))
function.name: formvar
function.intro: Phase 4 generalises the Phase 3 form panel from `Hlr | Llr` to every complex type that carries a `<ui:form>` annotation in `tools/project.xsd`. The XSD additions for `StpFixture` and `TestFile` plus the schema-driven attribute/child split in `buildOperations` mean the JSON Patch shape for any new payload is a schema change, not a TypeScript change.

llr.text: `FormPayloadKind` shall be widened from the closed Phase 3 union (`'Hlr' | 'Llr'`) to `string`, accepting any complex- type name returned by the sidecar's `ui_hints_index` (e.g. `SddModule`, `StpFixture`, `TestFile`, `Test`). The form deriver in `derive_form_schema` is already payload-agnostic; widening the consumer type is what unlocks the call sites.

`buildOperations(params, formData, fields?)` shall consult the schema-derived `fields` array — `kind === 'attr'` for attributes, `kind === 'child'` for child elements — to decide whether each form key becomes an `@attr` JSON Patch member or a child element body. The Phase 3 `id`/`name` heuristic shall remain as a fallback when `fields` is omitted so existing callers keep working unchanged.

`tools/project.xsd` shall publish `<ui:form>` annotations on `StpFixture` (attrs `name` required, `source` optional) and `TestFile` (attrs `path` required, `role` and `count` optional) so the form deriver can produce a JSON Schema for each. Neither type carries a `<ui:treeNode>` annotation because the existing tree projection already surfaces their contents (artefacts, individual `<test>` entries) under their parent groups.

function.title: Phase 4 add commands and project bootstrap ([tools/vscode-project-xml/src/commands/forms.ts](../tools/vscode-project-xml/src/commands/forms.ts))
function.name: bootstrap
function.intro: Four new add commands (`addModule`, `addStpFixture`, `addTestFile`, `addTest`) plus the empty-workspace bootstrap command (`projectXml.initProject`) round out the "no hand-written XML on the critical path" surface for SDD modules, STP fixtures, test files, individual tests, and brand-new projects. A seven-step Walkthrough makes the flow discoverable from VS Code's Get Started page.

llr.text: `projectXml.addModule` shall append a new `<module>` under `/sdd/modules/`, `projectXml.addStpFixture` shall append a new `<fixture>` under `/stp/integration_environment/`, and `projectXml.addTestFile` shall append a new `<file>` under `/tests/`. Each command shall open the same `FormPanelProvider` keyed on the corresponding XSD complex type — no per-payload TypeScript beyond the append-path constant.

`projectXml.addTest` shall present a `vscode.QuickPick` over every existing `<tests>/<file>` element and shall append the new `<test>` to the picked file's path via the JSON Patch `/tests/file[path=<picked>]/test/-`. When no `<file>` elements exist the command shall surface a warning that points the user at `addTestFile` rather than silently failing.

`projectXml.initProject` shall collect `name`, `short_name` (validated against `/^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,15}$/`), and `author` (default `TBD`) via `vscode.window.showInputBox` and shall invoke the sidecar's `init_project` method. On success the command shall open the new `Project.xml` in the editor, the new `PVD.md` in side-by-side preview, and shall refresh the Project Spec tree. On a "file exists" error the command shall offer a modal Overwrite prompt and re-call with `force: true` on confirmation.

`tools/vscode-project-xml/package.json` shall declare a `contributes.walkthroughs[]` entry with id `projectXml.welcome` and exactly seven steps in this order: `init`, `addHlr`, `addLlr`, `addModule`, `addTest`, `lint`, `render`. Each step's `completionEvents` shall reference the matching `onCommand:projectXml.*` event so VS Code marks the step done as soon as the user runs the command. Every command referenced from a `completionEvents` entry shall be declared under `contributes.commands`.

function.name: packaging
function.intro: Phase 6 turns the extension from a "checkout-bound" tool into a self-contained `.vsix` that works in any workspace. A `prepackage` build step bundles every Python file the sidecar spawns into `dist/python/` inside the extension; a new `projectXml.scaffoldTools` command (also chained from `projectXml.initProject`) drops a copy into the workspace's `tools/`, so brand-new repositories are immediately self-contained for CLI, CI, and contributors who do not have the extension installed.

llr.text: The `tools/vscode-project-xml/package.json` `scripts.prepackage` entry shall recursively copy `tools/project_io.py`, `render_doc.py`, `lint_project.py`, `project_edit.py`, `project_merge.py`, `project.xsd`, the `templates/` directory, and the `ai/` package (when present) from the TraceR `tools/` source tree into `tools/vscode-project-xml/dist/python/`. The script shall overwrite any pre-existing `dist/python/` so each package build starts from a clean copy, then install the required runtime Python dependencies (`defusedxml`, `jinja2`, `lxml`) into the same `dist/python/` directory so the bundled sidecar can start without any workspace-local pip install. The `tools/vscode-project-xml/.vscodeignore` file shall not exclude `dist/python/`, so the bundled tree survives `vsce package`.

`getToolsDir()` in `tools/vscode-project-xml/src/util/paths.ts` shall, when no workspace folder contains the configured `<projectXml.toolsDir>` (default `tools/`), fall back to `context.extensionUri.fsPath + '/dist/python'`. The fallback shall apply only when the bundled directory exists on disk; if neither the workspace nor the bundle resolve, the path helper may still return the configured workspace path, but sidecar startup MUST fail fast with an actionable `project_io.py not found at ...` error instead of a generic spawn `ENOENT`. `getProjectIoPath()` and the sidecar spawn shall use the returned path as `cwd` unchanged.

`tools/vscode-project-xml/package.json` `activationEvents` shall include `onCommand:projectXml.initProject` and `onCommand:projectXml.scaffoldTools` in addition to the existing `workspaceContains:doc/Project.xml` trigger so the extension activates and the bootstrap / scaffold flows are runnable in an otherwise-empty workspace.

`projectXml.scaffoldTools` shall recursively copy every file under `<extensionPath>/dist/python/` into the workspace folder's `<projectXml.toolsDir>` (default `tools/`), preserving the relative directory layout. Files that already exist in the workspace shall be skipped by default; when at least one such file is found, the command shall present a single `vscode.window.showWarningMessage` modal with `Overwrite all`, `Skip existing`, and `Cancel` choices, and shall honour the user's selection. The command shall surface a single status notification on completion listing the count of files written, skipped, and overwritten.

`projectXml.initProject` shall, on the success path of the sidecar's `init_project` call, check whether the target workspace folder contains a `<projectXml.toolsDir>` directory. When absent, it shall invoke `projectXml.scaffoldTools` automatically (no further prompt — the user has already opted into bootstrap) so the new workspace is self-contained immediately after init. When present, it shall not touch the existing `tools/`.

The `prepackage` script shall read the source `tools/project.xsd` and write the value of its `xs:schema/@version`-equivalent attribute (the `Project.xml` `schema_version` baseline the bundled XSD accepts) into `tools/vscode-project-xml/dist/python/.bundle_version` as a single line of plain UTF-8 text. The file shall ship inside the `.vsix` alongside the bundled `project.xsd`.

At extension activation, when the workspace contains a `<projectXml.toolsDir>/project.xsd` and the bundled `dist/python/.bundle_version` exists, the extension shall parse both `schema_version` values and, when the bundled version is strictly greater than the workspace's, surface exactly one `vscode.window.showInformationMessage(..., 'Re-scaffold tools/', 'Dismiss')` notification per session offering to re-run `projectXml.scaffoldTools` with overwrite confirmed. The notification shall never escalate to a warning or error, shall never block activation, and shall not appear at all when the bundled version is equal to or older than the workspace's. The workspace's `tools/` shall remain authoritative for the sidecar spawn at all times.

The extension shall contribute a status-bar item (`tools/vscode-project-xml/src/statusBar.ts`) that, on every lint run, displays `Project Spec: <n> error(s) / <m> warning(s)` sourced from `LintDiagnosticsProvider`'s latest `LintResult`. Clicking the item shall open `doc/Project.xml` (when known) and focus the Problems panel via `workbench.action.problems.focus`. When `projectXml.warningsAsErrors` is true the displayed total shall escalate warnings into the error count and the badge shall use the error background colour; the underlying warnings shall NEVER be suppressed in the Problems panel, the diagnostics collection, or the tooltip's verbatim breakdown (HLR-042). The status bar shall re-render when `projectXml.warningsAsErrors` changes.

llr.text: A `.github/workflows/publish-vsix.yml` workflow shall trigger on GitHub Release creation (`release: types: [created]`), install Node 20 LTS and Python 3.12, run `npm ci && npm run prepackage && npm run build && npm run compile && npm run test:unit`, stamp the `package.json` version from the release tag (`npm version "${TAG#v}" --no-git-tag-version`), then run `npx @vscode/vsce package` and attach the resulting `.vsix` to the GitHub Release via `gh release upload`. A final `npx @vscode/vsce publish` step shall run only when a `VSCE_PAT` repository secret is defined; in its absence the workflow stops at the asset upload so the maintainer remains the explicit gate on Marketplace publication.

`tools/vscode-project-xml/media/` shall hold every Marketplace-listing asset (`icon.svg` for the activity bar, `icon.png` at 128×128 for the listing tile, at least three screenshots under `screenshots/`, and an optional `walkthrough.gif`). The directory shall include a `README.md` listing the required files, their dimensions, and the capture procedure so a release maintainer can refresh assets without reading the SDD; the per-step walkthrough markdown files (`media/walkthrough/0N-*.md`) referenced by the `walkthroughs` contribution shall remain in place. Binary placeholders are not committed for the PNG/GIF assets — the README documents the gap so a future release step can populate them before `vsce publish`.

`scripts/prepackage.js` shall copy the repository-root `images/screenshots/` directory into `dist/images/screenshots/` so that the User Manual's relative `../images/screenshots/` paths resolve correctly when the manual is served from `dist/python/User_Manual.md` inside the packaged `.vsix`. The copy shall be skipped silently when the source directory does not exist.

`scripts/prepackage.js` shall install the third-party runtime Python dependencies imported by the bundled toolchain (`defusedxml`, `jinja2`, `lxml`) into `dist/python/` alongside the copied TraceR sources, preferring the workspace `.venv` interpreter when present and otherwise falling back to `python3`/`python` on PATH. A missing interpreter or pip-install failure shall fail packaging with an explicit error message.

function.title: Structured three-way merger ([tools/project_merge.py](../tools/project_merge.py), [tools/vscode-project-xml/src/merge/MergeConflictResolver.ts](../tools/vscode-project-xml/src/merge/MergeConflictResolver.ts))
function.name: merge
function.intro: Phase 5.5 (HLR-034..036): the deterministic Stage A merger plus the AI-assisted Stage B residual resolver. The Python side preserves comments, CDATA, attribute order; unions disjoint adds and `<traces>` rows; reallocates colliding ids; and emits residual `Conflict` records the TS resolver feeds through the `merge.*` AI intents. The merge editor remains the sole commit surface — neither layer ever writes to `doc/Project.xml` automatically (per SDP §5.9).

llr.text: `merge_three_way(base, ours, theirs, *, xsd_path)` in `tools/project_merge.py` shall accept either filesystem paths or in-memory XML (`str`/`bytes`) for each of the three sides, shall preserve XML comments, CDATA sections, and attribute order across the merge (via `lxml.etree`), and shall return a `MergeResult` with `merged_xml`, `residual_conflicts`, `lint`, `auto_resolved`, and (when applicable) `refused`/`refusal`. When `base` is `None` or empty the function shall not raise — it shall return `refused=True` with a human-readable `refusal` string so the resolver can degrade gracefully (HLR-034).

The merger shall walk a fixed container registry covering `hlrs/section/hlr@id`, `llrs/function/llr@id`, `tests/file/test@name`, `sdd/modules/module@path`, and `stp/fixture@id`. For each container it shall: union additions whose keys do not collide; auto-resolve one-sided edits and one-sided deletes; emit a `body` conflict for two-sided body edits; emit a `modify_delete` conflict when one side modifies and the other deletes; emit an `id_collision` conflict (with a proposed `rename_to`) when both sides add a different payload under the same key; and emit a `trace` conflict when field-level merge cannot reconcile divergent `<traces>` children. `<traces>` rows shall be unioned by the `(target, ref)` tuple in all auto-resolved cases.

After each merge the function shall recompute `<metadata>/<counts>` (`hlrs`, `llrs`, `tests`, `modules`, `fixtures`) from the merged tree so the per-document totals remain truthful regardless of which side last edited the counts block. A divergent `project/@schema_version` shall become a `schema_bump` residual conflict; a one-sided bump shall be promoted automatically.

`apply_resolution(merged_xml, conflict, resolution)` shall substitute a Stage-B payload (an AI `merge.*` intent response or a manual edit) back into the merged tree by locating the container via the `Conflict.container` XPath-ish address and replacing the matching element (or, for `schema_bump`, overwriting the `project/@schema_version` attribute). The function shall remain a pure transform — it shall never write to disk; the merge editor commits the final bytes (SDP §5.9).

`tools/project_io.py` shall expose `merge_three_way` and `apply_merge_resolution` JSON-RPC methods registered in the single `METHODS` table. Both methods shall be reachable when `projectXml.ai.enabled=false` so Stage A always runs; neither method shall raise on a missing/empty `base` — the refusal payload shall be returned as a successful result (HLR-034). Neither method shall write to `doc/Project.xml`.

`tools/ai/registry.py` shall declare four merge intents — `merge.body`, `merge.trace`, `merge.rename`, `merge.schema_bump` — each with `kind="merge"` and slash `resolve-conflicts`. `tools/ai/pipeline.py` shall return `AiResult(kind="merge_resolved", response=<parsed JSON>)` for any intent of kind `"merge"` from both `run()` and `evaluate()`, skipping the JSON-Patch translator and `apply_edit` write entirely.

`tools/vscode-project-xml/src/merge/MergeConflictResolver.ts` shall, on the `projectXml.resolveMergeConflicts` command and the `@projectspec /resolve-conflicts` slash command, (a) detect a Git MERGE state on `doc/Project.xml` via `vscode.extensions.getExtension('vscode.git').exports.getAPI(1)`, (b) read the `:1`/`:2`/`:3` blobs via `git show`, (c) call the sidecar's `merge_three_way`, (d) when `projectXml.merge.aiResidualResolution` is on AND `projectXml.ai.enabled` is on, drive each residual through the matching `merge.*` intent and substitute via `apply_merge_resolution`, and (e) present the merged candidate to the user. The resolver shall never write to `doc/Project.xml` without an explicit user accept gesture (HLR-036).

For every AI-suggested residual resolution the resolver shall append exactly one record to `<workspace>/.edit_doc/ai_history.jsonl` capturing `intent`, `conflict_kind`, `conflict_key`, sha-1 hashes of `base`/`ours`/`theirs`, the model rationale (when present), and the model id; provenance writes shall be best-effort and shall not block the resolution flow.

function.title: AI translators and gap.fix cascade ([tools/ai/translators.py](../tools/ai/translators.py))
function.name: ai_translators
function.intro: Phase 5b: response translators that convert structured AI JSON into JSON Patch operations consumable by apply_edit. The gap.fix translator supports cascading creation — when an upstream entity (module, HLR, LLR) is missing, the AI can produce nested new_module/new_hlr/new_llr blocks that are translated bottom-up so each parent exists before the child referencing it is appended.

llr.text: translate_gap_fix shall support cascading creation: when the AI response includes new_module, new_hlr, or new_llr blocks, the translator shall emit operations for them in parent-first order (module, then HLR, then LLR, then the primary test/LLR) so each element exists before child elements reference it.

llr.text: Placeholder refs (, , ) in trace arrays shall be resolved to the allocated ids/paths from the corresponding cascaded creation block before being emitted as operations, so the final XML contains valid cross-references.

llr.text: next_free_llr_id shall discover the established prefix by inspecting existing LLRs under the named function element. When an established prefix exists (e.g. PPD from LLR-PPD-01), new ids shall reuse it; when no LLRs exist yet, the prefix shall be derived from the function name, sanitized to [A-Z0-9] and truncated to 4 characters.

`pipeline.record_exchange()` shall write a `.bundle.json` (intent, target, next-free-ids, schema excerpt) and `.response.json` (parsed model response) pair when `TRACER_AI_RECORD_DIR` is set; when unset, recording shall be a no-op returning `None`.

`test/test_ai_integration.py` shall load each curated fixture from `test/fixtures/ai_recordings/`, translate the response to JSON Patch operations, apply them via `apply_edit` with `expect_clean=True`, and assert that placeholder references (`$new_llr`, `$new_hlr`, `$new_module`) are resolved to allocated IDs and the resulting XML contains the expected elements.

function.title: Humble object logic modules ([tools/vscode-project-xml/src/](../tools/vscode-project-xml/src/))
function.name: humble
function.intro: Phase 10: pure logic modules extracted from VS Code providers via the humble object pattern. Each module is free of `vscode` imports and testable in a plain Node process.

llr.text: `treeLogic.ts` shall export `TreeNodeDescriptor`, `decorate`, `renderLabel`, `labelSeverity`, `groupSeverity`, `buildLocator`, `filterTraces`, `propagateBadgeSeverity`, and `buildTopLevelDescriptors` as pure functions consuming only `ParsedProject` and `UiHintsIndex` types — no `vscode.*` imports — so tree-structure and label logic is unit-testable without a VS Code host.

No `vscode.*` imports shall appear in the logic module.

`lintMapping.ts` shall export `mapFindingSeverity`, `findingToDescriptor`, and `resultToDescriptors` as pure functions translating sidecar `LintResult` objects to `DiagnosticDescriptor` arrays without referencing `vscode.DiagnosticSeverity`, so severity mapping logic is testable in isolation.
