test.name: test_installs_tracer_skill_file
test.purpose: Pins LLR-INI-05: `init_project` writes `.github/skills/tracer/SKILL.md` from the bundled template and reports the path in the result payload.

test.name: test_load_known_metadata_id
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-PPD-01 and LLR-RND-02: `load_project` accepts a custom `xml_path` and selects the requested metadata id, returning the populated project namespace templates consume.

test.name: test_load_unknown_metadata_id_raises_project_xml_error
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-RND-02: an unknown metadata id raises `ProjectXmlError` rather than falling through to a partial render or `KeyError`.

test.name: test_missing_file_raises_project_xml_error
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-PPD-02: a missing input file raises the library's `ProjectXmlError`, not `SystemExit` or a bare `FileNotFoundError`, so JSON-RPC handlers can map it to a JSON-RPC application error.

test.name: test_malformed_xml_raises_project_xml_error
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-PPD-02: `xml.etree.ElementTree.ParseError` from a truncated `<project><unclosed>` document is wrapped as `ProjectXmlError` with the original cause preserved.

test.name: test_returns_jsonable_dict
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-PPD-04: the `parse_project_to_dict` projection round-trips through `json.dumps` — no `SimpleNamespace` instances may leak into the JSON-RPC surface.

test.name: test_default_metadata_for_first_document
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-PPD-03: with no `metadata_for` argument, the parser picks the first `<metadata><document>` entry (the skeleton's `SDD` row).

test.name: test_explicit_metadata_for_overrides
test.purpose: Verifies the `metadata_for` argument path of LLR-PPD-01 / LLR-PPD-03: an explicit id (`HLRs`) overrides the first-document default.

test.name: test_render_hlrs_returns_markdown_with_single_trailing_newline
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-RND-03: `render_document` returns Markdown with exactly one trailing newline (never zero, never two), so the CLI, sidecar, and preview pane all emit byte-identical output.

test.name: test_missing_template_raises_project_xml_error
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-RND-01: a missing template path raises `ProjectXmlError` rather than silently rendering an empty document.

test.name: test_writes_relative_schema_location_when_unset
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-INI-04: when the caller does not supply `schema_location`, `init_project` writes a relative (never absolute) `xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation` resolving to `project.xsd`, so XSD-aware editors find the schema with no further configuration.

test.name: test_explicit_schema_location_overrides_default
test.purpose: Verifies the explicit override path of LLR-INI-04: an explicit `schema_location` argument is written verbatim into the skeleton's `xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation`.

test.name: test_rendered_document_uses_gh_slug_anchor
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-RND-04: rendering an HLRs document end-to-end exercises the `gh_slug` filter and the `project.*` cross-reference indexes; if either were missing the render would have raised before producing output.

test.name: test_gh_slug_filter_is_registered_on_jinja_env
test.purpose: Pins LLR-RND-04 directly: a one-shot probe template that pipes a string through `gh_slug` round-trips to the expected slug, and the underlying `_gh_slug` helper produces the same value when called directly.

test.name: test_list_documents_returns_one_entry_per_metadata_document
test.purpose: Pins LLR-MET-02: bootstraps a fresh project with `init_project`, calls `render_doc.list_documents`, and verifies that every `<metadata><document>` becomes one dict in the returned list with the conventional template / output paths resolved when the optional attrs are absent.

test.name: test_list_documents_honours_explicit_template_and_output
test.purpose: Pins LLR-MET-01: a hand-rolled `Project.xml` whose `<document>` carries explicit `template=` and `output=` attributes is enumerated by `list_documents` with those values returned verbatim, proving the schema accepts the optional attrs and the resolver honours them.

test.name: test_ui_hints_surface_on_parsed_hlr
test.purpose: Pins LLR-HNT-02 and LLR-HNT-03: a hand-rolled `Project.xml` with `xmlns:ui="urn:tracer:ui:v1"` and `ui:icon`/`ui:color` attributes on an `<hlr>` is parsed by `parse_project_to_dict` so the decorated HLR's `ui` field carries `{"icon": ..., "color": ...}` while a sibling without hints carries `None`.

test.name: test_ui_hints_surface_on_parsed_llr_and_test
test.purpose: Pins LLR-HNT-02 and LLR-HNT-03 for the LLR and Test payload paths: `ui:icon` on `<llr>` and `ui:icon`/`ui:group` on `<test>` survive through `parse_project_to_dict` and appear under `flat_llrs[*].ui` and `flat_tests[*].ui` with the recognised keys preserved (including `group`, which the consumer ignores but the data contract carries).

test.name: test_xsd_accepts_ui_namespace_attributes_on_payload_elements
test.purpose: Pins LLR-HNT-01: a hand-rolled `Project.xml` with `xmlns:ui="urn:tracer:ui:v1"` and `ui:icon`/`ui:color`/`ui:group` attributes on `<hlr>`, `<llr>`, and `<test>` elements validates clean against `tools/project.xsd` via lxml's `XMLSchema.assertValid`, proving the `<xs:anyAttribute>` declarations on the payload complex types accept arbitrary `ui:*` attributes without rejecting the file.

test.name: test_cli_sed_edit_no_runtime_service
test.purpose: Verify that a user can modify Project.xml using a plain CLI text tool (sed), then render and lint the result using only local files under version control, with no database, network service, or proprietary format required.

test.name: test_ui_hints_applied_to_tree_and_form_panels
test.purpose: Verifies HLR-004: UI-hint annotations (ui:treeNode, ui:form, ui:lens) from the schema are consumed by the extension to render tree nodes, form panels, and code lenses without per-payload TypeScript code.

test.name: test_schema_version_attribute_exists_on_project_root
test.purpose: Verifies that the project.xsd schema defines a schema_version attribute on the <project> root element and that a valid Project.xml exposes it.

file.header: Tests for the importable surface of tools/lint_project.py: the `lint` entry point, the `Findings` dataclass, and the human-readable `Findings.report` formatter consumed by both the CLI and the JSON-RPC sidecar.

test.name: test_lint_returns_findings_object
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-LNT-01: `lint` returns a `Findings` instance (not a tuple, not a dict) so callers consume `.errors`, `.warnings`, `.notes`, and `.ok` by attribute.

test.name: test_findings_to_dict_is_jsonable
test.purpose: Verifies that `Findings.to_dict()` is JSON-serialisable (it is the JSON-RPC `lint` method's return shape) and contains exactly the documented `errors`/`warnings`/`notes` keys, each holding a list.

test.name: test_skeleton_has_no_errors
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-INI-01 and LLR-LNT-02: a freshly-bootstrapped `Project.xml` lints with zero errors (warnings for empty payloads are acceptable).

test.name: test_missing_file_records_error_no_stderr
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-LNT-04: `lint` is a pure function — a missing file is recorded as a `Findings.errors` entry, never written to stderr; redirected stderr remains empty.

test.name: test_malformed_xml_records_error
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-LNT-02: structural validation runs first; a malformed XML document records an error finding and short-circuits the semantic checks instead of producing a cascade of misleading "unknown id" diagnostics.

test.name: test_real_repo_project_xml_lints
test.purpose: Smoke test against the live `doc/Project.xml`: the project's own source-of-truth must lint with zero error findings (warnings for unbuilt-phase coverage gaps are acceptable per HLR-014/HLR-042).

test.name: test_report_writes_to_supplied_stream
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-LNT-04 and HLR-042: `Findings.report` writes errors, warnings, and notes verbatim to the caller-supplied stream and ends with a `N error(s)` summary line — warnings are surfaced, never silently dropped.

test.name: test_report_suppresses_warnings_when_disabled
test.purpose: Verifies the explicit `show_warnings=False` API: callers (CI scripts, CLI flag) can opt out of warning text in the report stream, but the warnings remain in the underlying `Findings` collection so the JSON-RPC surface still sees them.

test.name: test_malformed_xml_records_error_and_returns_none
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-VST-01: structural validation runs first; a malformed XML payload short-circuits the validator chain, records a `malformed XML` error, and returns `None` so semantic checks do not run on a broken tree.

test.name: test_lxml_path_is_preferred_when_available
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-VST-01: when `_try_lxml_validate` succeeds, `validate_structure` does not consult `xmllint` and emits no degraded-mode note.

test.name: test_xmllint_fallback_when_lxml_unavailable
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-VST-02: when `lxml` is unavailable, `validate_structure` falls back to `_try_xmllint_validate` and proceeds without emitting the structural-only note.

test.name: test_structural_only_emits_explicit_note
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-VST-03: when neither `lxml` nor `xmllint` is available, `validate_structure` returns the well-formedness-only tree and records exactly one explicit note saying that XSD validation was skipped.

test.name: test_bad_hlr_id_format_is_an_error
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-SEM-01: an HLR id that does not match `HLR-NNN` is reported as a hard error naming the offending id and the expected pattern.

test.name: test_bad_llr_id_format_is_an_error
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-SEM-01: an LLR id that does not match `LLR-XXX-NN` is reported as a hard error naming the offending id and the expected pattern.

test.name: test_duplicate_hlr_id_is_an_error
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-SEM-02: every duplicate `HLR-NNN` id is reported as an error naming the duplicated id.

test.name: test_duplicate_llr_id_is_an_error
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-SEM-02: every duplicate `LLR-XXX-NN` id is reported as an error naming the duplicated id.

test.name: test_unknown_hlr_trace_is_an_error
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-SEM-03: an LLR whose `<trace target="HLR" ref="..."/>` cites a non-existent HLR id produces an error quoting the missing id.

test.name: test_unknown_llr_trace_from_test_is_an_error
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-SEM-03: a test whose `<trace target="LLR" ref="..."/>` cites a non-existent LLR id produces an error quoting the missing id.

test.name: test_non_dotted_sdd_ref_is_a_warning_not_an_error
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-SEM-04: an SDD trace `ref` that does not match a dotted section pattern produces a warning rather than an error, reflecting that SDD section ids are weakly resolvable.

test.name: test_coverage_gap_for_uncovered_llr_is_a_warning
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-SEM-05 and LLR-LNT-03: an LLR with no test traces produces exactly one `has no test verifying it` warning and no error finding.

test.name: test_coverage_gap_for_uncovered_hlr_is_a_warning
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-SEM-05 and LLR-LNT-03: an HLR with no direct test and no LLR-mediated coverage produces a `has no test verifying it` warning rather than an error.

test.name: test_hlr_covered_indirectly_via_llr_test_is_not_a_gap
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-SEM-05: an HLR is considered covered when at least one of its LLRs has a test, so no gap warning is emitted in the indirect-coverage case.

test.name: test_missing_metadata_document_is_a_warning
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-SEM-06 and LLR-MET-04: a `<metadata>` block whose `<document>` declares an id whose conventional template (`tools/templates/<id>.md.j2`) is absent from disk produces a `missing-template` warning naming both the document id and the absent path; documents whose template does exist do not.

test.name: test_duplicate_metadata_document_is_an_error
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-SEM-06: duplicate `<document id="..."/>` entries within `<metadata>` are reported as errors naming the duplicated id.

test.name: test_xsd_reserves_ui_namespace_prefix
test.purpose: Pins LLR-MET-05 and HLR-056: the shipped `tools/project.xsd` declares `xmlns:ui="urn:tracer:ui:v1"` on its schema root, reserving the namespace prefix for the future UI hint registry without requiring any further toolchain change.

file.header: Tests for the JSON-RPC surface in tools/project_io.py. Exercises both the in-process handle_request() entry point and the end-to-end stdin/stdout subprocess form (the SubprocessTests class spawns the real `python3 tools/project_io.py` so it covers the same wire path the VS Code extension uses).

test.name: test_lint_method_returns_findings
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-SRV-07 and HLR-016: the `lint` method dispatches through the registry, returns a JSON-RPC response with `result` containing `errors`/`warnings`/`notes`/`ok`, and echoes the request's `id`.

test.name: test_lint_matches_cli_findings
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-SRV-07 and HLR-043 (cross-surface output equivalence): the in-process `lint_project.lint` library and the JSON-RPC `lint` method return byte-identical errors/warnings/notes for the same `Project.xml`.

test.name: test_render_method_returns_markdown
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-SRV-07 and LLR-RND-03: the `render` method delegates to `render_document` and returns a `result` whose `output` ends with exactly one newline and whose `out_path` is `null` when no `out` parameter is supplied.

test.name: test_render_writes_to_out_path
test.purpose: Verifies the `out` parameter path of LLR-SRV-07 and LLR-RAL-01: when `out` is supplied, the sidecar writes the rendered Markdown to that path and echoes the path in `result.out_path`.

test.name: test_parse_to_json_returns_dict
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-SRV-07 and LLR-PPD-04: the `parse_to_json` method delegates to `parse_project_to_dict` and the response round-trips through `json.dumps`.

test.name: test_init_project_method
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-SRV-07, LLR-INI-01, and LLR-INI-05: the `init_project` method delegates to `render_doc.init_project`, writes the new files (`Project.xml`, `PVD.md`, `.github/skills/tracer/SKILL.md`), and echoes the destination paths in the response.

test.name: test_init_project_refuses_overwrite
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-INI-03 and LLR-SRV-04: `init_project`'s overwrite guard surfaces as a JSON-RPC `APPLICATION_ERROR` (-32000) rather than as a server crash.

test.name: test_unknown_method_returns_method_not_found
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-SRV-03: an unknown method name produces JSON-RPC `METHOD_NOT_FOUND` (-32601) per the spec.

test.name: test_missing_method_returns_invalid_request
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-SRV-03: a request object with no `method` key produces JSON-RPC `INVALID_REQUEST` (-32600) per the spec.

test.name: test_invalid_params_returns_invalid_params
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-SRV-04: a `render` call missing required parameters surfaces as JSON-RPC `INVALID_PARAMS` (-32602), distinguishing user error from sidecar bug.

test.name: test_application_error_for_bad_xml_path
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-SRV-04: a `render` call against a non-existent `xml_path` surfaces as JSON-RPC `APPLICATION_ERROR` (-32000) so the client can distinguish a fixable user error from an `INTERNAL_ERROR` (-32603) sidecar bug.

test.name: test_notification_returns_none
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-SRV-05: a JSON-RPC notification (`jsonrpc=="2.0"`, no `id`) returns `None` from `handle_request` so the serve loop emits no response line for it.

test.name: test_multiple_requests_one_per_line
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-SRV-01 and LLR-SRV-05: `serve` processes line-delimited requests in order and writes one response per line, with the response `id` matching the request `id` for each.

test.name: test_invalid_json_returns_parse_error
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-SRV-03: a non-JSON line produces JSON-RPC `PARSE_ERROR` (-32700) per the spec.

test.name: test_blank_lines_ignored_and_eof_returns_zero
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-SRV-02: `serve` ignores blank input lines (no response is written for any of them) and returns exit code 0 on EOF — the documented clean-shutdown path the VS Code extension relies on.

test.name: test_methods_registry_contains_documented_methods
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-SRV-06, LLR-SRV-07, and LLR-MET-03: the `METHODS` registry table holds exactly the documented method names (`lint`, `render`, `parse_to_json`, `list_documents`, `init_project`) and every value is callable.

test.name: test_dispatch_routes_through_methods_table
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-SRV-06: registering a stub handler at runtime makes a brand-new method dispatchable through `handle_request` without any change to the dispatcher — proving the dispatcher consults `METHODS` rather than a hard-coded if/elif chain.

test.name: test_unknown_method_after_unregister_returns_method_not_found
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-SRV-06: removing a method from the registry makes it unreachable (`METHOD_NOT_FOUND`) without any code change in `handle_request` — the symmetric proof that dispatch is registry-driven.

test.name: test_echo_lint_request_returns_findings
test.purpose: End-to-end integration test that spawns the real `python3 tools/project_io.py` subprocess, sends one JSON-RPC `lint` request on stdin, and verifies the response on stdout (LLR-SRV-01, HLR-016, HLR-021). This is the acceptance path the VS Code extension's `ProjectIoClient` exercises in production.

test.name: test_subprocess_lint_matches_in_process_lint
test.purpose: Cross-surface equivalence pin (HLR-043): the spawned `python3 tools/project_io.py` subprocess returns byte-identical errors and warnings to the in-process `lint_project.lint` library for the same `Project.xml`.

file.header: Tier-1 (Mocha + ts-node, no VS Code host) unit tests for the schema-driven document discovery surface in tools/vscode-project-xml/src/util/documents.ts. Uses a fake `ProjectIoClient` whose `listDocuments` returns a fixed set so cache, lookup, and path-resolution can be exercised without spawning the Python sidecar.

test.name: returns the document list from the sidecar verbatim
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-BLD-01 and LLR-MET-02: `loadDocuments(client)` returns the document set produced by the sidecar's `list_documents` method in the same order, with no in-TypeScript filtering.

test.name: caches the result per client and reuses it
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-BLD-01: `loadDocuments` caches the discovered set per client (the second call returns the same array reference and the sidecar is invoked once), so per-keystroke consumers do not fan out into N parallel sidecar calls.

test.name: invalidateDocumentsCache forces a re-fetch
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-BLD-01: `invalidateDocumentsCache(client)` drops the cached set so the next `loadDocuments(client)` call re-queries the sidecar — the contract used by the on-save and on-refresh handlers in `activate`.

test.name: picks up a new schema-driven document with no source edit
test.purpose: Pins HLR-054 and HLR-055 directly: a fake sidecar configured to return one extra `Plan` entry causes `loadDocuments` to surface it in the runtime set with its `template` and `output` paths intact, proving that adding a `<metadata><document>` entry is sufficient for the extension to recognise a new generated document with no TypeScript change.

test.name: returns the entry with a matching id
test.purpose: Verifies the lookup contract used by `renderAndPreview` and the preview content provider: `findBaselineDocument(docs, id)` returns the entry whose id matches.

test.name: returns undefined for an unknown id
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-RAP-01: `findBaselineDocument` returns `undefined` for an unknown id so `renderAndPreview` can refuse with a warning toast rather than fall through to a partial render.

test.name: templatePath joins workspaceRoot with the doc-relative template
test.purpose: Verifies the path-join contract behind LLR-RAL-01 / LLR-MPP-01: `templatePath(workspaceRoot, doc)` resolves to `<workspaceRoot>/<doc.template>` so the sidecar render call sees a usable absolute path under the schema-driven workspace-relative template attribute.

test.name: sourcePath joins workspaceRoot with the doc-relative output
test.purpose: Verifies the path-join contract behind LLR-RAL-01: `sourcePath(workspaceRoot, doc)` resolves the `output` attribute against the workspace root so `renderAll` writes to the expected on-disk path.

test.name: templatePath returns absolute paths verbatim
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-MET-01 and LLR-RAL-01: when the document declares an absolute `template=` attribute, `templatePath` returns it unchanged, proving the schema's optional override survives the path resolver and is not silently relocated under the workspace root.

test.name: sourcePath returns absolute output paths verbatim
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-MET-01 and LLR-RAL-01: when the document declares an absolute `output=` attribute, `sourcePath` returns it unchanged, so a project can render a document outside the workspace root without the resolver getting in the way.

file.header: Tier-1 (Mocha + ts-node, no VS Code host) unit tests for the lint-driven badge index in tools/vscode-project-xml/src/util/badges.ts. Drives `buildBadgeIndex` with hand-rolled `LintFinding` arrays so the projection from finding messages onto HLR / LLR ids and the error-wins-over-warning rule are pinned without spawning the Python sidecar.

test.name: marks HLR ids cited by warnings with ⚠
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-BDG-01 and LLR-BDG-02: a single warning finding citing `HLR-001` produces the `'⚠'` badge for that id under the `'hlr'` tag.

test.name: marks LLR ids cited by warnings with ⚠
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-BDG-01 and LLR-BDG-02: a warning finding citing an `LLR-XXX-NN` id produces the `'⚠'` badge for that id under the `'llr'` tag.

test.name: marks ids cited by errors with ❌
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-BDG-02: an error finding citing an HLR id produces the `'❌'` badge.

test.name: errors win over warnings when both cite the same id
test.purpose: Pins the severity-ordering rule in LLR-BDG-02: when the same id appears in both a warning and an error finding (in either order), the badge is always `'❌'`.

test.name: returns undefined for ids that no finding mentions
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-BDG-02: ids no current finding cites have no badge, so the tree provider emits an undecorated label.

test.name: ignores notes (info-only findings carry no badge)
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-BDG-01: `note`-severity findings (informational, e.g. validator-path notes) do not contribute to the badge set, so the tree is not cluttered by ids that lint did not flag as a real problem.

test.name: handles undefined items (no lint result yet)
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-BDG-03: `buildBadgeIndex(undefined)` returns an empty `BadgeIndex`, so the tree provider can call `setBadges` unconditionally during the initial load before the first lint run completes.

test.name: does not return a badge for unrelated tags (test, file)
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-BDG-02: only `'hlr'` and `'llr'` tags carry a badge today; lookups for `'test'` or `'file'` always return `undefined` so future lint findings on those tags can be added without changing existing tree behaviour.

test.name: extracts every id mentioned in a single message
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-BDG-01: a single finding message that mentions both an HLR id and an LLR id (e.g. a broken-trace error) badges both ids, matching the existing `rangeForFinding` extraction rules used by the diagnostics provider.

test.name: exposes the raw severity for callers that need finer control
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-BDG-02: `BadgeIndex.severityFor(tag, id)` returns the underlying severity (`'error'` / `'warning'` / `undefined`) so future consumers (status-bar item, AI surfaces) can branch on the raw severity without parsing the emoji badge.

file.header: Tier-1 unit tests for the UI hint registry consumer in tools/vscode-project-xml/src/util/hints.ts. Drives `applyHintsToNode` against a minimal `vscode.TreeItem` mock so the icon / color decoration path is pinned without spawning a VS Code host.

test.name: returns false and leaves iconPath untouched for null / undefined hints
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-HNT-04: `applyHintsToNode` is a no-op when the upstream parsed payload had no `ui` field at all (`null` or `undefined`), so the tree provider can invoke it unconditionally on every leaf.

test.name: returns false when no recognised key is present
test.purpose: Verifies the recognised-key gating in LLR-HNT-04: a hint payload that carries only the reserved `group` key (no `icon`) must produce no decoration today, since `group` is accepted-and-ignored.

test.name: returns false when icon is the empty / whitespace string
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-HNT-04 and the matching guard in LLR-HNT-02: `icon=""` or `icon=" "` is treated as absent, so a malformed payload cannot install a blank `ThemeIcon` on the tree node.

test.name: sets a ThemeIcon when icon is provided
test.purpose: Verifies the happy path of LLR-HNT-04: with a recognised `icon` value, `applyHintsToNode` installs `node.iconPath = new ThemeIcon(icon)` and returns `true`.

test.name: tints the ThemeIcon with a ThemeColor when color is provided
test.purpose: Verifies the color-tint leg of LLR-HNT-04: when both `icon` and `color` are present, the constructed `ThemeIcon` carries a `ThemeColor` whose id matches the supplied string.

test.name: trims surrounding whitespace from icon and color
test.purpose: Verifies the whitespace-trim guarantee of LLR-HNT-04: leading / trailing spaces on `icon` and `color` are stripped before constructing the `ThemeIcon` / `ThemeColor`, so authoring noise does not produce an invalid icon name.

test.name: treats whitespace-only color as absent (icon only, no tint)
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-HNT-04: a payload with a real `icon` but a whitespace-only `color` produces an untinted `ThemeIcon`, never a `ThemeColor` constructed from an empty string.

test.name: ignores `group` while still honouring icon when both are set
test.purpose: Pins the reserved-key contract from HLR-058 and LLR-HNT-04: an extra `group` key on the payload does not block the `icon` decoration, so files can carry `ui:group` for a future grouping pass without losing today's icon support.

test.name: replaces a pre-existing iconPath when hints fire
test.purpose: Verifies the override path of LLR-HNT-04: when the tree provider has already assigned a default `iconPath` and a hint payload then fires, the hint icon replaces the default rather than being silently dropped.

file.header: Tier-1 unit tests for the regex-based locator in tools/vscode-project-xml/src/util/locator.ts. Drives the locator with a hand-constructed XML sample under a FakeTextDocument so the assertions cover real ranges without standing up a VS Code host.

test.name: targets the id="..." attribute, not the whole element
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-RVX-02: `findIdRange` returns a range over the `id="..."` attribute value (not the whole tag), so the diagnostic underline and the reveal cursor land on the meaningful token.

test.name: disambiguates between elements that share an id substring
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-RVX-02: the `\bid="ID"` anchoring distinguishes ids whose values overlap as substrings, so HLR-001 cannot be misreported as the location of HLR-002 (and vice versa).

test.name: returns undefined when the id is not present

test.name: findAttrRange locates a test by name

test.name: findElementRange locates the opening tag of a payload

test.name: prefers HLR ids over other tokens in the message

test.name: falls back to LLR id when no HLR matches

test.name: returns undefined when no workspace folder is open

test.name: picks the folder that contains the configured xmlPath
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-PTH-01: in a multi-root workspace, `getProjectFolder` picks the folder whose root contains the configured `xmlPath`, not just the first folder in the list.

test.name: falls back to the first folder when no folder contains Project.xml

test.name: resolves relative settings against the project folder

test.name: returns absolute settings verbatim

test.name: returns undefined for every helper when no workspace folder is open

test.name: names the missing Project.xml when folders are open

file.header: Tier-1 unit tests for the line-framing and dispatch path of ProjectIoClient in tools/vscode-project-xml/src/sidecar.ts. The framing is driven directly by feeding bytes to the private onStdout hook and probing the private pending map; this keeps the tests host-free and independent of the spawned Python sidecar.

test.name: dispatches a complete response line to the matching pending request
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-PIC-02: pending resolvers are keyed by the response `id`, so a complete response line resolves exactly the matching pending promise and clears it from the in-flight map.

test.name: reassembles a response split across multiple chunks
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-PIC-02: the line buffer reassembles a JSON response that arrives split across multiple stdout chunks before dispatching it to the resolver.

test.name: dispatches multiple responses arriving in one chunk in id order
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-PIC-02: multiple responses delivered in a single stdout chunk are split on the newline boundary and dispatched to the correct resolvers, even when responses are returned out of request order.

test.name: rejects with SidecarError when the response carries an error object
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-PIC-03: a JSON-RPC error response surfaces as `SidecarError(code, message)` so callers can switch on the JSON-RPC error code without parsing message text.

test.name: ignores blank lines and unknown ids without disturbing pending requests
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-PIC-02: stray notifications and blank lines on the sidecar's stdout do not accidentally resolve a pending request.

test.name: logs invalid JSON lines and continues without rejecting any pending request
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-PIC-04: invalid JSON arriving on the sidecar's stdout is logged to the `Project Spec` `OutputChannel` and the dispatcher continues processing without rejecting any in-flight request.

test.name: failAll rejects every pending request with the supplied error
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-PIC-03: when the sidecar process exits unexpectedly, every pending request is rejected with the same exit error rather than hanging the caller.

test.name: dispose rejects pending requests with a "sidecar disposed" error
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-PIC-05: `ProjectIoClient.dispose` rejects every pending request with a `sidecar disposed` error so callers do not leak promises across extension deactivate.

test.name: carries the JSON-RPC error code on a named SidecarError instance
test.purpose: Verifies the `SidecarError` constructor contract that LLR-PIC-03 depends on: the error carries the JSON-RPC `code`, identifies as `SidecarError` via its `name`, preserves the `message`, and is an `Error` subclass.

file.header: Tier-1 unit tests for the pure Quick Fix helpers in tools/vscode-project-xml/src/codeActions/fixes.ts: Finding.code recognition, message parsers, id allocators, and stub builders. Drives every helper without spawning a VS Code host so the SDP §8 Phase 2.5c contract that fixes route on Finding.code (never on payload element name) is pinned at the lowest tier.

test.name: lists exactly the four Phase 2.5c codes
test.purpose: Pins LLR-QFX-02: the Quick Fix code set is exactly `{broken-trace, id-format, missing-template, no-test}` so adding a fifth code is a deliberate edit to fixes.ts rather than an accidental drift.

test.name: isFixableCode accepts the four codes and rejects others
test.purpose: Pins LLR-QFX-02: the type guard accepts the four codes and rejects unknown / empty / non-string inputs so the dispatcher cannot accidentally route an unfixable diagnostic.

test.name: parses broken-trace HLR messages
test.purpose: Pins LLR-QFX-03: `parseBrokenTrace` extracts the trace target (HLR) and the bad ref token from the linter's error message verbatim.

test.name: parses broken-trace LLR messages
test.purpose: Pins LLR-QFX-03 and LLR-QFX-05: `parseBrokenTrace` recognises an `LLR` target without any payload-name branching, so the same picker code path serves both HLR-side and LLR-side broken traces.

test.name: parses id-format messages for HLRs
test.purpose: Pins LLR-QFX-03: `parseIdFormat` extracts the `kind` (`HLR`) and the malformed id from the linter's `<hlr id="..."> does not match HLR-NNN` message.

test.name: parses id-format messages for LLRs and extracts the prefix
test.purpose: Pins LLR-QFX-03: `parseIdFormat` infers the function-name prefix (`PCL`) out of a malformed `LLR-PCL-1` so the renumber Quick Fix preserves the function the malformed id belongs to.

test.name: parses missing-template messages
test.purpose: Pins LLR-QFX-03: `parseMissingTemplate` pulls the `<document>` id and the workspace-relative template path the linter said is missing.

test.name: parses no-test messages for HLRs and LLRs
test.purpose: Pins LLR-QFX-03 and LLR-QFX-05: `parseNoTest` recognises an orphan whether it is an HLR or an LLR, so the stub-test fragment is built from the same code path for both.

test.name: next free HLR id picks max+1 with preserved width
test.purpose: Pins LLR-QFX-03: `nextFreeHlrId` returns `HLR-NNN` zero-padded to the widest existing id so the renumber Quick Fix preserves the project's id-width convention.

test.name: next free LLR id keeps the requested prefix
test.purpose: Pins LLR-QFX-03: `nextFreeLlrId('PCL', existing)` only counts ids matching the requested prefix when computing max+1, so renumbering an LLR-PCL never reuses an LLR-OTHER number.

test.name: stubTestFragment cites the orphan via a payload-agnostic <trace>
test.purpose: Pins LLR-QFX-03 and LLR-QFX-05: the stub-test fragment carries one `<trace target="..." ref="..."/>` whose `target` is the orphan kind passed in (HLR or LLR), proving the no-test fix never names HLR or LLR specifically in its emitted text.

file.header: Tier-1 unit tests for the payload-agnostic CodeActionProvider in tools/vscode-project-xml/src/codeActions/QuickFixProvider.ts. Drives the dispatcher with hand-rolled `vscode.Diagnostic` instances so each Finding.code surfaces exactly the right Quick Fix command — and asserts the provider source contains no payload element name, pinning the SDP §8 Phase 2.5c contract at the lowest tier.

test.name: contributes only the QuickFix code action kind
test.purpose: Pins LLR-QFX-02: the provider declares only `CodeActionKind.QuickFix`, so VS Code never asks it for refactor or source actions outside its scope.

test.name: exposes a fix table keyed exactly on the four Finding.codes
test.purpose: Pins LLR-QFX-02: the static `FIX_TABLE` keys are exactly the four Phase 2.5 codes, so a contributor cannot register a fifth fix without a deliberate table edit.

test.name: returns a Quick Fix for each Finding.code (broken-trace)
test.purpose: Pins LLR-QFX-02 and LLR-QFX-04: a `broken-trace` diagnostic surfaces a Quick Fix whose command is `projectXml.fix.replaceTraceRef` and whose kind is `quickfix`.

test.name: returns a Quick Fix for id-format
test.purpose: Pins LLR-QFX-02 and LLR-QFX-04: an `id-format` diagnostic surfaces the renumber Quick Fix.

test.name: returns a Quick Fix for missing-template
test.purpose: Pins LLR-QFX-02 and LLR-QFX-04: a `missing-template` diagnostic surfaces the stub-template Quick Fix.

test.name: returns a Quick Fix for no-test
test.purpose: Pins LLR-QFX-02 and LLR-QFX-04: a `no-test` diagnostic surfaces the stub-test Quick Fix.

test.name: ignores diagnostics from other sources (eg redhat.vscode-xml)
test.purpose: Pins LLR-QFX-02: diagnostics whose `source` is not `'projectXml'` are ignored, so the Quick Fix table never fires on redhat.vscode-xml errors that happen to share a code value.

test.name: payload-agnostic: a `<plan>`-shaped diagnostic still routes by code
test.purpose: Pins the SDP §8 Phase 2.5c contract restated in LLR-QFX-02: a diagnostic whose message references the `<plan>` payload but carries `code = broken-trace` produces the same Quick Fix as one citing an HLR/LLR — the dispatcher sees only the code.

test.name: source contains no payload element name
test.purpose: Pins LLR-QFX-02: a static check on the QuickFixProvider source proves it contains no `<plan>`, `<hlr>`, `<llr>`, `<test>`, `<sdd>`, or `<stp>` token, mechanically enforcing the "never on payload element name" constraint instead of relying on review.

file.header: Acceptance test for the SDP §8 Phase 2.5c contract: triggering each Finding.code value on the `<plan>` fixture surfaces the correct Quick Fix and applying the fix produces a clean re-lint. Each case mutates a copy of test/doc/Project.xml to introduce exactly one finding code, applies the equivalent text edit (mirroring what vscode.WorkspaceEdit would produce), and asserts the linter is clean afterwards.

test.name: test_broken_trace_quick_fix_clears_finding
test.purpose: Pins LLR-QFX-01, LLR-QFX-04, LLR-QFX-05: a malformed HLR ref triggers a `broken-trace` finding; replacing the ref with a valid HLR id (the `WorkspaceEdit.replace` the picker would emit) produces a clean re-lint.

test.name: test_id_format_quick_fix_clears_finding
test.purpose: Pins LLR-QFX-01, LLR-QFX-03, LLR-QFX-04: an `<hlr id="HLR-1">` triggers an `id-format` finding; renumbering the id (and any incoming traces) as the next free `HLR-001` produces a clean re-lint.

test.name: test_missing_template_quick_fix_clears_finding
test.purpose: Pins LLR-QFX-01, LLR-QFX-03, LLR-QFX-04: a `<document>` row whose template file is absent triggers a `missing-template` finding; creating the file with the stub content produces a clean re-lint.

test.name: test_no_test_quick_fix_clears_finding
test.purpose: Pins LLR-QFX-01, LLR-QFX-03, LLR-QFX-04: an HLR with no test verifying it triggers a `no-test` warning; appending the stub `<file><test><traces>` block before `</tests>` produces a clean re-lint.

file.header: Phase 3 tests for tools/project_edit.py — apply_edit and the JSON-Schema deriver. Builds an in-tmpdir Project.xml with a CDATA-bearing HLR, a comment, and a covering test, then exercises every supported operation kind plus the validate-then-write contract.

test.name: test_replace_attribute_writes_when_clean
test.purpose: Pins LLR-AED-01 and LLR-AED-03: a `replace` op against `/hlrs/section[number=1]/hlr[id=HLR-001]/@name` rewrites the attribute and the file is written when the candidate lints clean.

test.name: test_replace_text_body_with_cdata
test.purpose: Pins LLR-AED-01: a text body containing markup-significant characters is wrapped in a `CDATA` section so subsequent renders see the same tokens the form submitted.

test.name: test_append_new_hlr
test.purpose: Pins LLR-AED-03: an `add` op against `/hlrs/section[...]/hlr/-` appends a new `<hlr>` element with the supplied attributes and child elements; the form-panel addHlr command path is exercised end-to-end.

test.name: test_failed_validation_leaves_file_byte_identical
test.purpose: Pins LLR-AED-02: an XSD failure (replacing an HLR id with a value that fails the HlrId pattern) leaves `xml_path` byte-identical to its pre-call state and surfaces the structured findings in the result.

test.name: test_broken_trace_blocks_write
test.purpose: Pins LLR-AED-02: a new LLR whose trace targets a non-existent HLR is rejected by the linter; the file is not written and the original bytes are preserved.

test.name: test_roundtrip_preserves_existing_cdata
test.purpose: Pins LLR-AED-01: editing an attribute on an element whose `<text>` child is wrapped in CDATA leaves the CDATA section verbatim in the rewritten file.

test.name: test_roundtrip_preserves_top_level_comment
test.purpose: Pins LLR-AED-01: top-of-file XML comments survive a successful round-trip write, proving lxml's parser/serializer is preserving the comment node verbatim.

test.name: test_next_free_hlr_id
test.purpose: Pins LLR-ADD-01: `next_free_hlr_id` returns the next HLR-NNN id (zero-padded to the widest existing id) so the addHlr command can pre-fill the form.

test.name: test_next_free_llr_id
test.purpose: Pins LLR-ADD-01: `next_free_llr_id` returns the next LLR-PREFIX-NN id for an existing function-prefix (preserving the established width).

test.name: test_next_free_llr_id_for_unseen_function
test.purpose: Pins LLR-ADD-01: `next_free_llr_id` for a fresh function prefix returns `LLR-PREFIX-01` so the addLlr command works on a brand-new function.

test.name: test_derive_hlr_form_schema_shape
test.purpose: Pins LLR-FRM-01: `derive_form_schema("Hlr")` returns a JSON Schema whose properties match the `<ui:form>` field list, lifts the HLR id pattern from the XSD `HlrId` simple type, marks `id`/`name` required, and selects the textarea widget for the cdata-kind text body.

test.name: test_derive_llr_form_schema_with_refs
test.purpose: Pins LLR-FRM-01: when a `refs` snapshot is supplied, the LLR `traces` array surfaces a populated `enum` for the `ref` selector so the form renders a closed-set picker.

test.name: test_split_path_strips_leading_slash
test.purpose: Pins LLR-AED-03: the path grammar parser strips the leading slash and rejects relative paths so a missing `/` is caught early in the apply_edit pipeline.

test.name: test_predicate_parses_attr_terms
test.purpose: Pins LLR-AED-03: predicates of the form `[k=v,k2=v2]` are parsed as ordered attribute terms so element selection by attribute combination works.

test.name: test_rename_llr_cascades_to_test_traces
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-AED-07: renaming an LLR id via apply_edit cascades the change to all trace ref attributes referencing the old id.

test.name: test_rename_hlr_cascades_to_llr_and_test_traces
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-AED-07: renaming an HLR id via apply_edit cascades to LLRs and tests.

test.name: test_trace_ref_enum_union_of_all_targets
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-FRM-12: _trace_array_schema produces a ref enum containing the union of all valid target ids.

test.name: test_trace_ref_no_enum_when_refs_empty
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-FRM-12: _trace_array_schema omits enum when no valid targets exist.

file.header: Phase 3 tests for the pure `buildOperations` helper exported from FormPanelProvider, the `computeCoverage` inline summary, `resolveFormParams` coverage-link navigation, plus `package.json` contribution-point assertions. Pins the JSON Patch shape the form panel posts to the sidecar without needing the VS Code webview API.

test.name: emits a single add op with @attr keys when in add mode
test.purpose: Pins LLR-FRM-03: in add mode the helper emits exactly one `add` op whose value uses the `@attr` / bare-key convention apply_edit understands.

test.name: emits one replace per attribute and per child in edit mode
test.purpose: Pins LLR-FRM-03: in edit mode the helper emits a separate `replace` op per attribute and per child element body.

test.name: drops empty trace name attributes
test.purpose: Pins LLR-FRM-03: trace rows with an empty `name` field are emitted without an `@name` attribute so the round trip does not introduce blank attribute noise.

test.name: skips invalid trace rows
test.purpose: Pins LLR-FRM-03: trace rows missing `target` or `ref` are filtered out so a half-edited row in the form does not produce a `<trace>` that fails XSD validation downstream.

test.name: throws when neither basePath nor appendPath is supplied
test.purpose: Pins LLR-FRM-03: missing both addressing modes is a programmer error that throws synchronously rather than producing an empty patch.

test.name: treats SddModule path/title as attributes and the rest as children
test.purpose: Pins LLR-FRM-06: when the schema-derived `fields` list marks `path` and `title` as `kind:'attr'`, the form-submission patch lifts them into `@path` / `@title` while keeping `purpose` and `responsibility` as child element bodies.

test.name: treats StpFixture name/source as attributes
test.purpose: Pins LLR-FRM-06 and LLR-FRM-07: the `<ui:form>` block on `StpFixture` declares `name` and `source` as attributes and the helper's add-mode patch reflects that.

test.name: treats TestFile path/role/count as attributes
test.purpose: Pins LLR-FRM-07: the `<ui:form>` block on `TestFile` declares `path`, `role`, and `count` as attributes; the helper emits all three under the `@`-prefix convention.

test.name: treats Test name as attribute and purpose as child body
test.purpose: Pins LLR-FRM-06: the `Test` complex type's `name` is an attribute while `purpose` and `traces` are children; the schema-driven split surfaces all three correctly inside the same `add` op.

test.name: falls back to the id/name heuristic when no fields are supplied
test.purpose: Pins LLR-FRM-06: callers that omit the `fields` argument retain the Phase 3 `id`/`name`-as-attribute behaviour so existing HLR/LLR call sites keep working unchanged.

test.name: emits replace ops for SddModule attrs and child fields in edit mode
test.purpose: Pins LLR-FRM-06 + LLR-FRM-14: in edit mode, buildOperations emits one replace op per attribute (@path, @title) and one per child element body (purpose, responsibility, data_structures, algorithm) when the fields array classifies them correctly.

test.name: emits replace ops for StpFixture attrs in edit mode
test.purpose: Pins LLR-FRM-06 + LLR-FRM-07: in edit mode, buildOperations emits replace ops for StpFixture's @name and @source attributes.

test.name: declares one walkthrough with seven steps in the documented order
test.purpose: Pins LLR-BOOT-04: the `contributes.walkthroughs[]` block declares exactly one walkthrough (`projectXml.welcome`) whose step ids appear in the order `init, addHlr, addLlr, addModule, addTest, lint, render`.

test.name: every walkthrough step references an existing command via completionEvents
test.purpose: Pins LLR-BOOT-04: each `completionEvents: ['onCommand:projectXml.X']` entry refers to a command that is also declared under `contributes.commands`, so VS Code can mark the step done when the command runs.

test.name: computeCoverage returns downstream LLRs and tests for an HLR
test.purpose: Pins LLR-FRM-08: when editing an HLR, `computeCoverage` produces a CoverageInfo with sections for downstream LLRs and direct tests, each test entry carrying a sublabel with the parent file path and a locator so the webview can post `openForm` messages.

test.name: computeCoverage returns upstream HLRs and tests for an LLR
test.purpose: Pins LLR-FRM-08: when editing an LLR, `computeCoverage` produces upstream HLR links (with sublabels) and verifying test links whose sublabel carries the test's parent file path.

test.name: computeCoverage returns upstream traces for a test
test.purpose: Pins LLR-FRM-08: when editing a test, `computeCoverage` lists both upstream HLRs and upstream LLRs from the test's `<traces>` block and includes the test's file path in the coverage summary.

test.name: computeCoverage returns HLRs tracing to an SDD module
test.purpose: Pins LLR-FRM-08: when editing an SDD module, `computeCoverage` lists HLRs whose `<traces>` contain `target="SDD" ref="<path>"`.

test.name: contributes the five expected commands to the tree view title menu
test.purpose: Pins LLR-PSP-08: validates that `package.json` declares exactly the five expected commands (refresh, lint, renderAll, resolveMergeConflicts, initProject) in the `view/title` menu contribution for `projectXml.tree`.

test.name: groups actions and project commands into separate menu groups
test.purpose: Pins LLR-PSP-08: validates that the `view/title` menu entries are split into `1_actions` (≥3 entries: Refresh, Lint, Render) and `2_project` (≥2 entries: Merge, Init) groups so VS Code renders a visual separator between them.

test.name: keeps refresh in the navigation group as an icon button
test.purpose: Pins LLR-PSP-08: validates that Refresh also appears in the `navigation` group so it is rendered as a visible icon button in the view title bar, in addition to appearing in the dropdown.

test.name: resolves an HLR locator to form params with correct basePath
test.purpose: Pins LLR-FRM-11: `resolveFormParams` maps `{tag:'hlr', value:'HLR-001'}` to an `OpenFormParams` with `type='Hlr'` and `basePath='/hlrs/section[number=N]/hlr[id=HLR-001]'`.

test.name: resolves an LLR locator to form params with correct basePath
test.purpose: Pins LLR-FRM-11: `resolveFormParams` maps an LLR locator to a form params object whose `basePath` addresses the correct `<llr>` inside its parent `<function>`.

test.name: resolves a test locator to form params with correct basePath
test.purpose: Pins LLR-FRM-11: `resolveFormParams` maps a test locator (with `attr:'name'`) to a form params whose `basePath` includes both the parent `<file>` path and the `<test>` name predicate.

test.name: resolves an SDD module locator to form params with child fields

test.name: resolves an STP fixture locator to form params

test.name: returns undefined for a non-existent fixture

test.name: returns undefined for a non-existent item
test.purpose: Pins LLR-FRM-11: when the locator targets an id that does not exist in the parsed project, `resolveFormParams` returns `undefined` rather than throwing.

test.name: returns undefined for an unknown tag
test.purpose: Pins LLR-FRM-11: when the locator's `tag` is not one of the recognised item types (`hlr`, `llr`, `test`, `module`, `fixture`), `resolveFormParams` returns `undefined`.

test.name: test_disjoint_adds_union
test.purpose: Pins LLR-MRG-02: when each branch adds a non-overlapping HLR to the same `<hlrs>/<section>`, the merger unions both adds with zero residual conflicts and `auto_resolved >= 1`.

test.name: test_traces_unioned_by_target_ref
test.purpose: Pins LLR-MRG-02: `<trace target ref>` rows added on both sides survive the merge, with no duplicates of pre-existing rows; `<traces>` are keyed by `(target, ref)`.

test.name: test_renames_theirs_side
test.purpose: Pins LLR-MRG-02: when both branches add a different payload under the same id, the merger keeps `ours` at the original id and emits one `id_collision` residual conflict whose `rename_to` allocates the next free id for the theirs side.

test.name: test_both_edited_body
test.purpose: Pins LLR-MRG-02: two-sided body edits surface as exactly one `body` residual conflict carrying the serialised ours/theirs XML for Stage B (no double-counting from the field-level merge fallback).

test.name: test_one_sided_body_change_takes_winner
test.purpose: Pins LLR-MRG-02: when only one branch edits a body (the other matches base) the merger auto-resolves to the changed side with no residual conflict.

test.name: test_modify_delete_surfaces_conflict
test.purpose: Pins LLR-MRG-02: a payload modified on one side and deleted on the other produces a `modify_delete` residual conflict.

test.name: test_no_base_refuses

test.name: test_empty_base_refuses

file.header: ExTester-based UI integration tests for editor-centric features: Reveal in XML, status bar lint summary, Problems panel diagnostics, and code lenses on Project.xml.

test.name: Reveal in XML opens Project.xml with HLR element selected
test.purpose: Verifies that "Reveal in Project.xml" from the tree context menu opens `doc/Project.xml` in the editor and selects the targeted HLR element's id attribute value.

test.name: status bar shows TraceR lint summary
test.purpose: Verifies the extension's status bar item is visible and displays error/warning counts in the format "TraceR: N errors / M warnings".

test.name: Problems panel shows lint findings for coverage gaps
test.purpose: Verifies that lint diagnostics appear in the VS Code Problems panel. The fixture includes an HLR with no downstream LLR (coverage gap), so the linter should report at least one warning.

test.name: code lenses appear on HLR elements in Project.xml
test.purpose: Verifies that coverage code lenses appear on HLR elements when `doc/Project.xml` is opened in the editor, and at least one lens contains coverage information (LLR/test counts).

file.header: ExTester-based UI integration tests for the AI tree context menu. Exercises the `gap.fix` intent flow: uncovered HLR visibility, context-menu "Run AI Action…" entry, and end-to-end intent picker → input → outcome.

test.name: HLR-T02 (uncovered) leaf is visible and has a context menu
test.purpose: Verifies that an uncovered HLR leaf (HLR-T02) is visible in the tree and can be right-clicked to open a context menu.

test.name: right-click on uncovered HLR shows Run AI Action… when AI is available
test.purpose: Verifies that right-clicking an uncovered HLR leaf shows "Run AI Action…" in the context menu when AI capabilities are available, confirming the `aiTargetable` contextValue token is set.

test.name: gap.fix flow: context menu → intent picker → input → outcome
test.purpose: Exercises the full gap.fix AI intent flow from the tree context menu through the intent picker and user input, verifying the end-to-end wiring of the AI tree menu surface.
